entries.name: Christopher Isherwood at the Grand Hotel
entries.summary: Christopher Isherwood (1904-1986) was a gay British writer, best known for his book Farewell to Berlin, later filmed as Cabaret.
entries.description: Christopher Isherwood (1904-1986) was a gay British writer, best known for his book Farewell to Berlin, later filmed as Cabaret. On November 30, 1934, Isherwood paid a visit to Malmö. In his autobiography "Christopher and his Kind" he mentioned how well he was received. He came to Malmö to give a lecture titled, "My Experiences in an English Film Studio". Before the lecture, Isherwood was taken to the Grand Hotel, where apparently he was given quite a lot to drink. He was fairly inebriated by the time of his lecture, but he quickly noticed that the audience was also drunk. The lecture was a success! Photo 1: from a postcard in a private collection. Photo 2: By National Media Museum from UK - W. H. Auden and Christopher Isherwood en route to China, 1938. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Malmö Östra Sjukhus (1935–1995)
entries.summary: Olga Börjesson was chief physician at Malmö s psychiatric hospital.
entries.description: Olga Börjesson was chief physician at Malmö s psychiatric hospital. In the early 1940s, 20 men were charged with "moral crimes" relating to homosexual acts, and two of them were, according to Börjesson, in need of mental health treatment. At the same time, a legislative proposal was being prepared, with the aim of decriminalizing homosexuality. The proposal committee noted that there was a lack of knowledge around female homosexuality, and so a group of experts, including Börjesson, were asked to answer a questionnaire. In her questionnaire, Böriesson described nurses and students who, when in love, had become either affectionate or jealous. She d noticed the latter emotion only in those in relationships with men. "For my part, I would think that female homosexuality is not a socially dangerous phenomenon in our country," she stated. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Dama-Verken
entries.summary: The company was actually called AB Damm- och Spånledningar, but no-one around here would ever say that: Dama-Verken was the name that stuck.
entries.description: The company was actually called AB Damm- och Spånledningar, but no-one around here would ever say that: Dama-Verken was the name that stuck. They started in 1909, and moved to newly built premises on Lantmannagatan in 1936. The office building and the machine hall were on the same site, as well as an air-raid shelter where the staff would park their bikes. And what did they make? Well, fans and ventilation shafts mostly, as well as some other equipment associated with air conditioning and drying. They also made those classic metal lockers made from sheet metal that have graced innumerable workplaces over the years. Photograph: Malmö-boken, 1946
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Saturnus
entries.summary: Founded in 1893, AB Fabriken Saturnus moved to their newly built premises on Lantmannagatan in 1937.
entries.description: Founded in 1893, AB Fabriken Saturnus moved to their newly built premises on Lantmannagatan in 1937. Offices, factories and warehouses were all set up here in the new industrial district. Designed by architect Stig F Johansson, the new building cost 200,000 kronor to build. The business was acquired by the Liepe family in 1920. Soft drinks were their main concern, but they also produced essences and seasonings derived from fruits and spices (their mulled wine mix was a big seller). Changes to licensing laws in 1995 enabled them to start making their own alcoholic beverages. Piratens Besk ( The Pirate s Bitters ) is one of their best known products. In 2000, the family business moved to Fosieby, on the outskirts of Malmö. Photography: Malmö-boken, 1946
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: AB Textilkonst
entries.summary: You don t hear about shoelace makers so often these days.
entries.description: You don t hear about shoelace makers so often these days. However, when this company started trading, back in 1932, shoelaces were their bread and butter (though they also made ribbons and lace). The shoelace business was booming apparently, because they built new premises on Norbergsgatan seven years later, incorporating both an office and a factory. The company was owned by the Ehnimb family, who were somewhat forward-thinking. The new home they built provided a decent environment for their workers modern, light, airy, with well-equipped lunch rooms and changing facilities. Their products developed over time, and they became well known for their lampshades (as well as their shoelaces). Photography: Malmö-boken, 1946
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Malmö Stadsarkiv
entries.summary: The City Archive (Malmö Stadsarkiv) is situated in the former premises of Arbetet newspaper.
entries.description: The City Archive (Malmö Stadsarkiv) is situated in the former premises of Arbetet newspaper. The Social Democrat publication was located in this building from 1939. Nowadays, the archive holds documents and pictures about Malmö's history, people and places. The collection contain material that reflects society's views on homosexuality and bisexuality throughout the years. This material includes documents from authorities such as the police and law courts, but also from organisations like RFSL Malmö and Lesbisk Front. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text adapted from: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Båstadsgården & Barnrikehusen
entries.summary: Båstadsgården, två hus som byggdes som bostadsrätter.
entries.description: Båstadsgården, två hus som byggdes som bostadsrätter. De två husen bakom är kända som Barnrikehusen och byggdes ca 1936. De var moderna hus med ljusa genomgående lägenheter med centralvärme, badrum med toalett, gasspis, sopnedkast, vind, källare och tvättstuga. För att få bo här krävdes minst tre barn i familjen. Här växte författaren Mary Andersson upp med föräldrar och sex syskon i en trerummare på 65 kvadratmeter. Foto Stadsarkivet

entries.name: Ekströms skomakeri
entries.summary: That s a shoemaker standing in his doorway greeting us.
entries.description: That s a shoemaker standing in his doorway greeting us. The door has been built over and the building has been significantly altered since the photograph was taken. Malmö's great Art Nouveau architect Oscar Hägg designed the building, which was completed in 1906. The stucco depicts, among other things, a vigilant owl and a cat playing with a ball of yarn. It was a beautiful facade, but the small apartments behind it were nothing special they lacked amenities and had an outdoor toilet in the backyard. The building originally had 34 one- and two-room apartments. In 1976, the balconies were taken down and most of the decorative facade was removed. Apartments were merged, and 34 became 19. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Nya Sofielundsskolan
entries.summary: Sofielund s old primary school sat beside an allotment site, Thulekolonin, which was set up in the 1910s.
entries.description: Sofielund s old primary school sat beside an allotment site, Thulekolonin, which was set up in the 1910s. The city of Malmö acquired the land in 1923, and earmarked it for future expansion of the school. It took a quarter of century for the expansion to take place Nya Sofielundsskolan ( The New Sofielund School ) was completed in 1949. Designed by Sture Fröl n, it s an example of the nyrealism architecture style that was popular in Sweden at the time. On opening, it was Sweden s largest school the dining room could seat 800 students. The bronze statue by the entrance is called The Magnifying Glass , and was made by Gustav Nordahl in 1953. One of the school s most notable former students is the adventurer Renata Chlumska. She was the first Swedish woman to climb Mount Everest. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Folkets Hus
entries.summary: In December 1947, the venerable Folkets Hus in Torpgatan (Sweden's first purpose built People s House) was replaced by a more modern structure on Nobeltorget.
entries.description: In December 1947, the venerable Folkets Hus in Torpgatan (Sweden's first purpose built People s House) was replaced by a more modern structure on Nobeltorget. Designed by Hans Westman, it provided a space for political and trade union activities, as well as a theatre. Södra Teatern (the Southern Theatre) was home to a branch of Malmö City Theatre, and it was a popular venue through the 1940s, 50s and 60s. Specialising in comedies and revues, Swedish theatre luminaries like Karl Gerhard, Povel Ramel Maritta Marke and Zarah Leander all performed there. Since 2006, it s been home to Moomsteatern a theatre company noted for its work with actors with learning disabilities. Photograph: Jeanette Rosengrens samling
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: AB Kvarnmaskiner
entries.summary: When it founded in 1867, this company was called Malmö Franska Kvarnstensfabrik Malmö French Millstone Factory even though it was actually Danish-owned.
entries.description: When it founded in 1867, this company was called Malmö Franska Kvarnstensfabrik Malmö French Millstone Factory even though it was actually Danish-owned. The French part of the name came from their use of French quartz, a development that had revolutionized the flour production industry. The millstones they produced were thus often known as fransyskor French girls. This nickname didn t seem to catch on outside of Sweden. They moved from near the harbour to these spacious premises (6400 m 2 ). They continued to trade until 1974, under their later name Kamas Kvarnmaskiner. Photograph: Malmö stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Folkets Funfair
entries.summary: From the beginning, the management had envisaged Folkets Park as a place with swings and carousels.
entries.description: From the beginning, the management had envisaged Folkets Park as a place with swings and carousels. There were more grown-up attractions in its early years, like test-your-strength games and shooting ranges, but only when the park expanded northwards was there enough space for a bone fide funfair. It arrived in 1926, with a funicular railway, ferris wheels, dodgems, and carousels. In a publication marking the park s 40th anniversary, one of its pioneering administrators, Nils Petter Hansson, said that the only facility in the world that matched Folkets Park was Coney Island in New York. There have been many rides in the park over the years, but in 2014 the management chose to stop renting out areas as amusement parks. Foto: Ur Jeanette Rosengrens samling
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Kürzels spinnerier
entries.summary: In 1896, Fritz K rzel opened a spinning mill here, named K rzels Fabriker AB.
entries.description: In 1896, Fritz K rzel opened a spinning mill here, named K rzels Fabriker AB. It became one of the largest in the city, producing dresses, rugs, and cloths for cleaning. In the 1940s, they had around 600 employees who benefited from a thoughtful personnel policy. For example, those with young children could bring them to work, where they would be put on to the company bus and driven to a Villa Midhem (close to where the motorway now enters Malmö) whereby they would be taken care of and brought back at the end of the working day. The building is also nicknamed Ugglanhuset (The Owl House), on account of the stone owl, just out of picture. Photography company Kungsfoto would later have their premises here for many years.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Malmö Central Prison (1914-2015)
entries.summary: In Sweden, homosexual acts were illegal until 1944.
entries.description: In Sweden, homosexual acts were illegal until 1944. Men were prosecuted for "fornication that is against nature". During the 20th century, there were three major lawsuits in Malmö, in which 34 men were prosecuted. The men were of varying ages, occupations, and social standings. In the last push, in 1940, 20 men were brought to trial. Four were sentenced to hard labour at the now closed Central Prison in Kirseberg. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Malmö Rådhus court
entries.summary: In 1940, around 20 gay men were prosecuted for "moral crimes" at the Rådhus Court.
entries.description: In 1940, around 20 gay men were prosecuted for "moral crimes" at the Rådhus Court. One of them was an aristocrat and former military officer. In a letter, he appealed for a conditional sentence as, "serving a sentence of imprisonment in front of my family would mean complete disaster". The sentence was two months' imprisonment, but the Court of Appeal changed it to a suspended sentence. Six months later, he took his own life. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Drottningtorget
entries.summary: Drottningtorget är uppkallat efter drottning Fredrika av Baden, gift med den svenske kungen Gustav IV Adolf.
entries.description: Drottningtorget är uppkallat efter drottning Fredrika av Baden, gift med den svenske kungen Gustav IV Adolf. Kungafamiljen bodde i staden i ett halvår 1806 07 och båda makarna biföll nådigt stadens önskan om att få uppkalla två torg efter dem. Vid platsen för torget hade tidigare stadens befästningsverk funnits och ännu tidigare stadens utpost åt öster, österport. Den 15 maj år 1900 öppnades stadens första saluhall i det gamla ridhuset som byggts redan 1819 åt husarregementet. 1965 blev det en privat samling av fordon som öppnade under namnet Vagnmuseum. Numera finns restaurang med fransk anknytning i huset, boulespel idkas och vi får väl anta att den glade vinnaren enligt tradition bjuder på pastis, laget runt. Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Maskinfabriks Aktiebolaget Thule
entries.summary: Formed in 1908, this company specialised in machine tools and, a little later, industrial planers and saws.
entries.description: Formed in 1908, this company specialised in machine tools and, a little later, industrial planers and saws. As they expanded, more room was needed, and in 1942 they built the large machine hall. Six years later, they built offices at the intersection of Lönngatan and Lantmannagatan. By the late 1950s, though, it was all over for Maskinfabriks AB Thule the business folded. Since then a steady flow of businesses have taken up the premises. åkermans used the space to build diggers and construction equipment. It was a vocational school for a while, then Malmö City Theatre moved in at the end of the 1970s and built props there. Since 2008, it s been home to Garaget, a library, cafe, and community meeting-place. Photograph: Malmö-boken, 1946

entries.name: Hollywood 1943
entries.summary: Efter första världskriget rådde akut bostadsbrist i Malmö och staden uppförde ett antal nödbostäder.
entries.description: Efter första världskriget rådde akut bostadsbrist i Malmö och staden uppförde ett antal nödbostäder. Bland annat byggdes dessa hus som uppfördes mellan Sorgenfrifarmen och renhållningsverket i början av 1920-talet. Husen skulle vara tillfälliga men blev kvar i många årtionden. Här bodde fattiga familjer med många barn under trånga omständigheter med enkelglas i fönstren och kallvatten i kranen. Det officiella namnet på träbarackerna var Sorgenfrihusen. I folkmun blev smeknamnen istället Hollywood, Klondyke, Beverly Hills, Pinnatorp, Pinnhusen och Diplomatstaden. Foto Okänd

entries.name: Konsthallstorget
entries.summary: On the left of the photograph, you can see Malmö s craft guild (Malmö Hantverksförening), which was designed in 1916 by the prolific architects Ewe and Melin.
entries.description: On the left of the photograph, you can see Malmö s craft guild (Malmö Hantverksförening), which was designed in 1916 by the prolific architects Ewe and Melin. To the right of the church opposite where Malmö Art Gallery currently stands lies the Johannes colonies (Johanneskolonierna). These were established in 1909 to provide both housing and leisure. Every colony (there were about 60 in total) comprised a small cottage and garden area, bordered with a small fence. The cottages would often have ornamental door and window frames in the snickarglädje style (snickarglädje literally means carpenter s delight ). The greenery you can see behind the fences on the right are likely the result of the hard work of the residents and visitors there. This all came to an end when Pilgården was built in 1943. Pilgården, which housed a restaurant and bowling alley, was inaugurated by prime minister Per Albin Hansson. The building still stands here today. Photograph: Jeanette Rosengren s collection

entries.name: Lars-Eric Tornberg 1921-1943
entries.summary: Lars-Eric Tornberg var en av 33 besättningsmän ombord på u-båten Ulven då den gick på en tysk mina utanför Marstrand i april 1943.
entries.description: Lars-Eric Tornberg var en av 33 besättningsmän ombord på u-båten Ulven då den gick på en tysk mina utanför Marstrand i april 1943. U-båten bärgades i augusti samma år och fördes in till Göteborg för en minneshögtid för de omkomna. Därefter sändes kvarlevorna av de unga männen till respektive hemorter. Ulvens historia har dokumenterats i artiklar, böcker och finns också med i handlingen i Bo Widerbergs sista film Lust och fägring stor där Björn Kjellman spelar en av de som förolyckades.

entries.name: The mountain roller coaster
entries.summary: From Arbetet newspaper, April 1944 The huge roller coaster in Malmö Folkets Park, whose silhouette provided a mountain landscape in Möllevången, no longer exists.
entries.description: From Arbetet newspaper, April 1944 The huge roller coaster in Malmö Folkets Park, whose silhouette provided a mountain landscape in Möllevången, no longer exists. On Saturday morning, it was completely destroyed by a fire that could have had catastrophic consequences under different conditions and without the fast, methodical response of the fire brigade. As it was, the fire was confined to the roller coaster itself. Somewhat surprisingly, the wooden frames of the carousels and miniature car track were saved, even though they sit close to where the fire broke out. There was also a sports hall underneath the roller coaster. After the fire, a bear cave, haunted house, and games arcade were built in their place. entries.description: Alfred Benzon AB grundades år 1900 och bestod av fem avdelningar: Kemikalieavdelningen - tillverkning av syror och gaser. Kolonialvaruavdelningen - tillverkning av bland annat bakpulver, puddingpulver , såskulör (soya), putsmedel och skurpulver. Kolonialavdelningen förpackade även icke-egentillverkade kryddor och essenser. Dessa gick under varunamnet Benzona. Maskinavdelningen - främst tillverkning och försäljning av Benzona Mjölkningsmaskin. Pennavdelningen - tillsyn, reparation och försäljning av pennor. Metallkemiska avdelningen - elektrolytisk oxidering av aluminium och lättmetall. Foto: Otto Ohm / Historisk bildbyrå / Malmö Museer

entries.summary: Furniture started to be made here in 1893, when master carpenter Anders Hult n opened his business (A Hult n AB).
entries.description: Furniture started to be made here in 1893, when master carpenter Anders Hult n opened his business (A Hult n AB). The company moved into a modern factory in 1947, on the corner of Norra Grängesbergsgatan and Kopparbergsgatan. The furniture made here was mostly for commercial use it would sit in department stores, banks, shops and offices, with customers all over the country. For more than twenty years after her husband's death, Emilia Hult n ran the business. Photography: Malmö-boken, 1946

entries.name: Anna 1860-1934 & Eva Bunth 1862-1947
entries.summary: Anna och Eva Bunth var pedagoger som ivrade för flickors utbildning.
entries.description: Anna och Eva Bunth var pedagoger som ivrade för flickors utbildning. 1887 grundade de en privatskola för flickor i Malmö och året därpå blev deras systrar, Clara och Frederique anställda som lärare. Brodern Oscar Albert blev också medarbetare. Skollokalerna byttes över tid. Man flyttade 1905 till den vackra byggnaden på Slottsgatan, ritad av Carl Ferdinand Rasmussen 1878. 88 elever fanns på skolan vid denna tid och kollegiet bestod av 13 lärarinnor och fyra lärare. De båda systrarna undervisade i olika ämnen; Anna i bibelläsning, biblisk historia, katekes, engelska och välskrivning. Eva undervisade i franska. Clara i sin tur hade hand om välskrivning och handarbete och Frederique hade uppsikt över skrivningarna. 1936 beslöt stadsfullmäktige att inrätta en kommunal flickskola i Malmö. De olika privatskolorna ombildades då och uppgick året därpå i Kommunala flickskolan.

entries.name: Kai finds love at Hipp
entries.summary: In the spring of 1949, Hipp aka Malmö Hippodrome welcomed Stockholm s Casino Revue.
entries.description: In the spring of 1949, Hipp aka Malmö Hippodrome welcomed Stockholm s Casino Revue. Their ensemble included Kai Gullmar, one of Sweden's great schlager composers. Gullmar, who according to Sydsvenskan, "trudged in and out of the sketches in her own style", found love here in the form of Danish-born Rita Rosenberg who worked in Hipp's ticket office. Rosenberg had previously performed as a dancer throughout Malmö. The two women began a relationship and Kai's composition First You Come, Then Nothing (Först Kommer Du Sen Ingentin) is dedicated to Rita. Foto 1: Av Photo by Jarl Ekenryd (TT) - Populär Historia, 2019:1, sid 41, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=78366679 Foto 2: Jeanette Rosengrens samling Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Per Albin Hansson bust
entries.summary: Emil Näsvall made this bust of Social Democratic politician Per Albin Hansson (1885 1946).
entries.description: Emil Näsvall made this bust of Social Democratic politician Per Albin Hansson (1885 1946). Hansson grew up in a house on the road which now bears his name Per Albin Hanssons Väg. The house has been turned into a museum in his memory. When he was 13 years old, his family moved from Fosie to the Korpen neighbourhood of Malmö. In his 20s, Hansson met his fianc e Sigrid Vestdahl, and moved to her home on Kristianstadsgatan, just a couple of paces from where his bust has stood since 1949. Per Albin Hansson was Prime Minister of Sweden twice, from 1932 to 1936 and from later that year until 1946. Foto 1: Ur Min ungdoms park Foto 2: Ur Svensk Damtidning

entries.name: Björngrottan
entries.summary: It's seems scarcely believable now, but as recently as the 1950s Folkets Park had its own bear cave.
entries.description: It's seems scarcely believable now, but as recently as the 1950s Folkets Park had its own bear cave. It was home to three bears Finn, Fina and Finette. From time to time (especially on warm summer days) a drunk person would fall into the bear pit but, somewhat extraordinarily, there were never any serious mishaps. Leftover cakes and pastries from the Far i Hatten cafe often ended up as bear food. Rather cakes than people, I suppose. Photograph: Bilder i syd, Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Anita and Hornet
entries.summary: The corner building here was home to Caf Hörnet (literally, The Corner Cafe).
entries.description: The corner building here was home to Caf Hörnet (literally, The Corner Cafe). When it was modernized in the 1950s, it became known as "Cozy Corner", the hub of the city's jazz life. The dots over the o on the neon sign disappeared at some point, and it became, simply, Hornet ( The Horn'). The building was demolished in the 1970s. One of the employees in its heyday was Anita (n e Tage) Nilsson who is said to be Malmö's first known trans person. Dressed in women's clothing, Anita was subjected to ridicule and harassment and was nicknamed Tage Tosa ( tosa is a Swedish homophobic slur). In the novel 'Q', Malmö author Fredrik Ekelund recounts a memory of how they made fun of "this creature with worn pumps, gray-black tights, a pale brown coat and a scarf on his masculine head. When they shouted: Tage! How s it going? , Anita replied in a determined feminine voice: My name is not Tage, my name is Anita! Ekelund also wrote of his own trans-identity,stating: "My name is not Fredrik, my name is Marisol". Foto 1. Lars Hector Foto 2 & 3. Bilder i syd Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Ghost train
entries.summary: From Max Lundgren's novel Inga Eliasson, Sales Assistant.
entries.description: From Max Lundgren's novel Inga Eliasson, Sales Assistant. The scene takes place on May 1, 1950 when Gunnar Sträng led the first of May celebrations: If only it had been Erlander! But that boring old man! In Folkets Park, the carousels spun, the chocolate wheels squeaked, the balloon bundles swayed in the wind, fastened to the salesmen's belts. There was screaming and life that surpassed all the markets Inga remembered from her childhood. Ole and Gösta Månsson walked arm-in-arm towards the bar, while the girls stood in line at the ghost train. Inga and Astrid disappeared into the darkness. The carriage swayed and rushed straight ahead towards a giant spider, which opened its arms to them with its long, hairy legs." Foto: Jeanette Rosengrens samling

entries.name: Oscar Winge 1884-1951
entries.summary: Oscar Winge, ursprungligen Svensson, var regissör, skådespelare och teaterchef i Malmö.
entries.description: Oscar Winge, ursprungligen Svensson, var regissör, skådespelare och teaterchef i Malmö. 1922 tog han över Hippodromen, en tidigare cirkusbyggnad, och gjorde om den till teater. Den drev han till 1944 då han överlät teatern till sin exhustru Elsa och blev lyrisk chef på den då nyinvigda Malmö stadsteater. I premiärföreställningen En midsommarnattsdröm spelade han själv rollen som Botten Vävare. I sin ungdom var Winge idrottsman och tävlade på hög nivå i såväl spjut som tresteg.

entries.name: Stora entrén
entries.summary: Folkets Park's main entrance on Amiralsgatan isn t its the oldest that can be found a short distance away on Norra Parkgatan.
entries.description: Folkets Park's main entrance on Amiralsgatan isn t its the oldest that can be found a short distance away on Norra Parkgatan. The park has had several different entrance buildings through the ages. The original was fairly plain and low, but it was replaced in 1952 by a fantastic 650m steel pipe construction, designed by Fritz Jaenecke and Sten Samuelsson. In 1985, the Social Democrats were voted out of power in Malmö for the first time in 66 years, to be replaced by a more conservative majority. A new entrance was built at this time, and the park s name changed from Folkets Park (literally, the people s park) to Malmö Park. The conservatory next to the entrance today was originally built at the Bo01 housing complex, at what is now Västra Hamnen. entries.name: Amiralen (from Amiralsgatan)
entries.summary: From Bo Widerberg's 1952 novel, Hösttermin: Then came Folkets Park, with the vibrant colours of its cramped carousels and Amiralen s exaggeratedly wide arch; mo
entries.description: From Bo Widerberg's 1952 novel, Hösttermin: Then came Folkets Park, with the vibrant colours of its cramped carousels and Amiralen s exaggeratedly wide arch; more than anything, the dancehall looked like an aeroplane hangar. But there the street widened, and became airy under the thick foliage of chestnut trees; you could imagine this is what a Parisian boulevard looked like. He remembered Amiralsgatan in the spring when the chestnuts swelled. When the sun shone on this street after the rain, it was perhaps more beautiful than any other in town. Foto: Jeanette Rosengren's samling

entries.name: Gustav Möller bust
entries.summary: On 24 August 1952, the bust of the former minister of social affairs and trade was unveiled in the presence of the man himself.
entries.description: On 24 August 1952, the bust of the former minister of social affairs and trade was unveiled in the presence of the man himself. Gustav Möller (1884-1970) was born in Malmö, grew up on Tallgatan (now Möllevångsgatan's extension to the west) and worked at the Social Democrat newspaper Arbetet, before becoming head of the book publisher Tiden. As minister of social affairs for four decades, he was involved in several social reforms; public dental care, child allowance, general national pension, and two weeks' holiday all bear his signature. The bust was carved in granite by the Skåne sculptor Ivar Johnsson. Foto: Bilder i syd

De fick tre gemensamma barn. Hilma Tjäder skrev boken Silfversmeden: berättelse om Kina om parets vardagsliv i ett land som dåförtiden fortfarande var tämligen okänt för västeurop er. entries.name: Naima Wifstrand
entries.summary: Naima Wifstrand (1890-1968) was one of Sweden's most famous actresses and operetta singers of the 20th century.
entries.description: Naima Wifstrand (1890-1968) was one of Sweden's most famous actresses and operetta singers of the 20th century. She came from a humble background in a foster family in Stockholm, but found education opportunities in the acting profession. She performed with Malmö Stadsteater late in her career, in the early 1950s, taking several acclaimed roles with Ingmar Bergman as director (she would go on to feature in a number of his films including Wild Strawberries and The Magician). She lived with the female sculptor and illustrator Ninnan Santesson, including a few years together in London. During her time in Malmö, Naima lived at Helmfeltsgatan 10. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Wikipedia commons

entries.name: Olga Hellquist 1893-1954
entries.summary: Olga Hellqvist spelade på scen såväl som på film, var också kuplettsångerska och komiker som började framträda på Folkets Hus teater 1914.
entries.description: Olga Hellqvist spelade på scen såväl som på film, var också kuplettsångerska och komiker som började framträda på Folkets Hus teater 1914. Samma år invigdes friluftsteatern i Pildammarna och några år senare kunde man se Olga spela där tillsammans med Edvard Persson. 1931 tog hon över det som kallades Teatercaf et vid Pildammsparken och i folkmun därpå kallat Olgas caf . Under några år på 30-talet var Olga teaterchef för Folkets Hus teater. Hit kom malmöbor i mängd, lockade av folklustspel, humor, sång och kupletter. Malmö Stadsteater invigdes 1944 med Shakespeares En midsommarnattsdröm. Det var man inte sena att utnyttja på Folkets Hus. Där satte man upp En sensommarnattsdröm med Olga i en roll som Thalia.

entries.name: Billie Holiday splits the crowd
entries.summary: In January 1954, Billie Holiday came to Malmö as the main attraction in a touring mini festival called "Jazz Club USA".
entries.description: In January 1954, Billie Holiday came to Malmö as the main attraction in a touring mini festival called "Jazz Club USA". The concert was held at Malmö FF s football stadium on Erikslustvägen, but reviews were mixed. Daily newspaper Sydsvenska Dagbladet described her renditions of "Willow Weep for Me" and "Strange Fruit" as exquisite , while jazz magazine Orkesterjournalen picked out My Man along with "Strange Fruit" as the concert s highlights. However, local publications Kvällsposten and Arbetet instead led with, Scandal at the jazz gala. They reported that her voice sounded tired and that she was so inebriated that she could barely stand. She wasn t helped by talking and laughing in the audience, they claimed.

entries.name: Höghuset
entries.summary: In 1953, the MKB housing association built an eight-storey building here, in the Fritz neighbourhood.
entries.description: In 1953, the MKB housing association built an eight-storey building here, in the Fritz neighbourhood. On the left of the picture you can see Sevedsgatan. Sevedsplan sits behind the high-rise building, on a patch of land that was previously an allotment garden, and a meadow before that. In the 50s, the neighborhood effectively became a small town within the city of Malmö, centred around Sevedsplan. The square housed a bakery, a tailor, a hairdresser, a florist, a tobacconist and a grocery store. When the area was built, cars were beginning to become more common and more thought was being given to traffic management. The city s policy involved building cul-de-sacs, in an attempt to reduce traffic in residential areas and make the streets freer for cyclists and pedestrians.

entries.name: Anna Stenberg 1867-1956
entries.summary: Anna Stenberg kom till Malmö i 20-årsåldern och arbetade som hospitalsköterska på asylen i Rundelsgatan, den tidens psykiatriska klinik.
entries.description: Anna Stenberg kom till Malmö i 20-årsåldern och arbetade som hospitalsköterska på asylen i Rundelsgatan, den tidens psykiatriska klinik. Hon gifte sig och fick tre döttrar, men blev tidigt änka och fick ensam försörja familjen. Snart engagerade hon sig i den unga arbetarrörelsen och fick flera uppgifter, bland annat blev hon sekreterare i Malmö Kvinnliga Diskussionsklubb. 1910 valdes hon som första kvinna in i Stadsfullmäktige. Sina sista år bodde Anna i den Dahlgrenska stiftelsen som revs 1978.

entries.name: Sture Lagerwall at Malmö Stadsteater
entries.summary: The first thing Sture Lagerwall did when he came to the theatre, was to go into the canteen, pull down his trousers, and lie face down on a table.
entries.description: The first thing Sture Lagerwall did when he came to the theatre, was to go into the canteen, pull down his trousers, and lie face down on a table. Nothing happened. Then he got up, buttoned up his trousers, and announced: And this shall be a theatre! In her 2012 book Mitt Malmö Stadsteater from 2012, Kristina Kamnert gleefully tells the story of how her fellow actor Sture Lagerwall introduced himself to new colleagues. As well as being an accomplished actor and film director, Lagerwall was a prot g and lover of legendary stage actor Gösta Ekman Snr. His recollections of his time at Malmö Stadsteater suggest that there were many gay men involved in its early years. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto 1: Postcard from private collection. Foto 2: Unknown photographer - http://www.malmostadsteater.se/site/mst/images/static/play/playimages/large/637/20120604115214.png, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=32281411

entries.name: Thekla Edstrand 1880-1959
entries.summary: Thekla Edstrand var konstsamlare och också den ledande gestalten i den kulturella salong hon drev i sitt hem på Slottsgatan 6.
entries.description: Thekla Edstrand var konstsamlare och också den ledande gestalten i den kulturella salong hon drev i sitt hem på Slottsgatan 6. Hit kom konstnärer som Isaac Gr newald och Ernst Norlind för att utbyta tankar med likasinnade. Thekla och hennes syskon delade också ut stipendier till unga, lovande konstnärer och på 50-talet öppnade hemmet som ett konstgalleri för allmänheten. I nästan 30 år kunde Malmöborna sålunda beskåda målningar, teckningar, grafik och skulpturer i detta privata museum. 1951 fick Thekla Edstrand medaljen Illis quorum. Den stiftelse hon startade delar fortfarande ut stipendier till unga, lovande konstnärer.

entries.description: Oscar Emil Hägg blev den mest kände jugendarkitekten i Malmö. Han var utbildad i Berlin och ritade många flerbostadshus i Rörsjöstaden, men bodde tillsammans med sin familj i ett egenritat hus på S. Parkgatan i Möllevången. De hus som Oscar ritat är kända för sitt pynt och utsmyckning, ofta i form av djur. Odd Fellowpalatset i hörnet av Engelbrektsgatan/Gustav Adolfs torg är ett av hans kända verk, liksom den fastighet på Lilla torgs norra sida som numera inrymmer ett hotell.

entries.name: Järnvägsövergången
entries.summary: From 1874, when the railway between Malmö and Ystad was opened, trains ran along what is now Lönngatan, and effectively divided the area into North and South Sofielund.
entries.description: From 1874, when the railway between Malmö and Ystad was opened, trains ran along what is now Lönngatan, and effectively divided the area into North and South Sofielund. In the photograph, you can see the raised barriers they would be brought down for passing trains and the car traffic would have to patiently wait. On the building, you can see a company name, Oskar Persson. The words down the sides of the door would give Swedish speakers a good idea of their line of business. Kött is the Swedish word for meat, and fläsk is pork. Oscar Persson is mentioned in östen Warnerbring s evocative tribute to the city, When Malmö Smelled (the song title sounds a lot better in the original Swedish När Malmö Doftade). Warnerbring was a celebrated singer, composer, and Eurovision Song Contest winner, born in Malmö in 1935. Here s a translation of some the lyrics: But among all the scents that had something, certainly I ve saved the best for last Oskar Persson came by on his magnificent horse In his butcher shop on wheels Then Malmö smelled, I don t forget, Of sausages and liver pate Then all the people smiled it felt good to be In Malmö, on a completely normal day

entries.name: Hotell Nornan
entries.summary: The legendary boundary-smashing trans person "Merry Lou", aka Marie-Louise Simonsen, ran the Hotell Nornan on Västergatan for a number of years in the 1960s.
entries.description: The legendary boundary-smashing trans person "Merry Lou", aka Marie-Louise Simonsen, ran the Hotell Nornan on Västergatan for a number of years in the 1960s. She also lived there. Marie-Louise was born a biological man, but underwent gender reassignment surgery at an early age. She came to Malmö in the 1960s, where she became well-known for her performances in amateur singing competitions. Her renditions of Zarah Leander songs were especially revered. Alongside Lars Hector she was a popular hostess and entertainer at both Gay House and Trocadero. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag

entries.summary: From 1960 to 1969, Rådhuskällaren was a place where the gay men of Malmö met in secret.
entries.description: From 1960 to 1969, Rådhuskällaren was a place where the gay men of Malmö met in secret. In the long bar in the basement, gay-friendly staff would serve Malmö's young gay men as they rubbed shoulders with older gentlemen, while businessmen, lawyers and other esteemed local figures ate in the adjacent dining room. entries.name: Kompanihuset
entries.summary: Huset byggdes under 1520-talet och har idag åter den engelskt röda färg som var dess ursprungliga.
entries.description: Huset byggdes under 1520-talet och har idag åter den engelskt röda färg som var dess ursprungliga. Förmodligen var det den danske kungens generalbyggmästare Marten Bussert som ritade huset. Antagligen var det tänkt som en sögningegård , en slags övernattningslägenhet för personer som var i kungens tjänst och snabbt behövde kunna nå Köpenhamn. Huset kom snart i det danska handelskompaniets ägo. Kompaniet var en fristad för handelsmän från övriga Danmark som var på tillfälligt besök. Här festade man, hit tog man sina varor och här höll man rådslag när det behövdes. Bild: Malmö kulturhistoriska förening

entries.name: Thilda Engström
entries.summary: a Here s a description of a typical Malmö woman who lived through the turn of the 20th century: Born Liatorp, Kronoberg County in 1868.
entries.description: a Here s a description of a typical Malmö woman who lived through the turn of the 20th century: Born Liatorp, Kronoberg County in 1868. In her late teens, she moved to Malmö to find a better life. Worked in the textile industry at Manufakturaktiebolaget and Malmö Yllefabriks Aktiebolag, among other factories. Married to manual worker Vilhelm, she would have a total of nine children. Widowed at age 43. Spent her later years living in a one-room apartment in Palmgatan 19. This is a summary of the life of Thilda Engström, who, despite some trying circumstances, lived to the age of 95. The house she lived in stood here, and was demolished in 1964 (the year after her death). The property built on this site went on to house the Swedish Employment Service (Arbetsförmedlingen) for many years. b This is a notice from the Social Democrat affiliated Arbetet newspaper in 1906 that illustrates the impact of poverty in this area. Here s the English translation: From the general public to those who are willing to make sacrifices. A worker by the name of Karl Lindahl, resident in Palmgatan, Sofielund, has been taken into Lund hospital after a long and very difficult illness. He has not been able to recover from his illness and his doctor has prescribed a stay in a sanatorium to regain his health. However, a shortness of sanatorium places means that this isn t possible. The man in question, who isn t a member of a health insurance association and has 3 young children, has had to apply for poverty relief [ fattigvård : the old Swedish equivalent of the poor laws and poorhouses]. His position is especially hard because he fell ill immediately after the long industrial action and strike in the building industry. Therefore, I dare to pray to those who consider themselves as having enough to be able rescue Lindahl, to send me a message. Additionally, it should be noted that the man s lifestyle is impeccable. Jöns Andersson, Storgatan 19, Sofielund c The house on the right was owned for a period in the 1990s by the Hell s Angels motorcycle club. In October 1996, a bomb planted by their rivals, The Bandidos, was detonated. The house was destroyed and a number of windows were smashed in the surrounding area.

entries.description: Hasselgatan was originally called Sturegatan, but together with several other streets nearby, it was renamed when Sofielund was incorporated in 1911. Since it was taken in 1967, it has been painted yellow, the door has been replaced, and it s generally been freshened up, but its still recognisable. These were drivers of the increasingly influential sobriety movement this was especially prominent in working class areas. Meetings would begin at 8 pm, so that the participants could get home from work and be able to eat their supper before attending. entries.description: Brewing had already been the family business for generations when Malmquists Bryggeriaktiebolag purchased a site and moved their business here in 1898. Fourteen years later, they were one of five Malmö breweries that merged to become AB Malmö Förenade Bryggerier, stepping up beer production from small-scale craftsmanship to large-scale industry. Oak barrels were replaced with enamel casks, and wooden stoppers made way for more modern variants. Drinks company Apotekarnes Vattenfabrik (literally, The Chemists Water Factory) moved here from the city centre, and were given the opportunity to produce Coca Cola under license in 1953. The business unsurprisingly expanded, and built new premises in 1961. Pripps bought the company shortly afterwards. The smell affected the students at Heleneholms school, opposite. Keeping the windows open during production was almost impossible.

entries.name: Ahoy, it’s the Rolling Stones!
entries.summary: The Rolling Stones came to Malmö a few days before their gigs at Baltiska Hallen the summer of 1965, and this photo shows Keith Richards, Mick Jagger and Brian
entries.description: The Rolling Stones came to Malmö a few days before their gigs at Baltiska Hallen the summer of 1965, and this photo shows Keith Richards, Mick Jagger and Brian Jones hitting the boutiques of östergatan. But according to writers Ulf Clar n and Staffan Olander, the fun really started later that day when the band headed out to sea. The concerts had been arranged by Britt Wadner, the indomitable boss of pirate radio station Radio Syd. Her commitment to commercial radio was absolute she was sent to jail on three occasions for refusing to shut down Radio Syd and her powers of persuasion were compelling. The Stones had a gap in their schedule after playing Copenhagen in June, and Britt somehow convinced them to stay in Scandinavia a little longer. The band were ferried out to Cheeta II, the home of the offshore station anchored between Sweden and Denmark. They did a press conference and interview, during which Brian revealed the extent of his shopping spree: We spent an awful lot of money. We went to a lot of shops. I bought about 20 to 30 sweaters, three coats, and about six pairs of shoes . Despite this shopping spree, photos suggest he actually spent most of his time in Malmö wearing a Radio Syd t-shirt. The actual concerts were somewhat underwhelming they only played for about 20 minutes each time and the amplifiers weren t powerful to overcome the noise of the crowd. Nevertheless, the visit was a huge success for Britt and Radio Syd: What a marketing coup! was the headline in the city s Kvällens Post newspaper.

entries.name: The Beatles’ frosty reception
entries.summary: On 14th October 1967, half of The Beatles popped up in Malmö.
entries.description: On 14th October 1967, half of The Beatles popped up in Malmö. Paul McCartney and George Harrison had come to Sweden to meet guru Maharishi Mahesh Yogi at Falsterbohus, a castle in the far south of Sweden. Hunger set in during the Flygbåtarna ferry ride from Copenhagen, so they and their entourage stopped off at Rådhuskällaren for lunch. It was, however, a rather formal establishment with a strict dress code. The Beatles weren t wearing ties so were refused entry. They continued to the Hotel Tunneln around the corner where they were greeted more warmly. In the age of Beatlemania, it was impossible for them to stay unnoticed for long: a passing journalist spotted them, and a crowd of local media soon descended on the hotel restaurant.

entries.name: The Beatles head home
entries.summary: George Harrison and Paul McCartney got a lot of media attention when they visited Maharishi Mahesh Yogi for a weekend in October 1967.
entries.description: George Harrison and Paul McCartney got a lot of media attention when they visited Maharishi Mahesh Yogi for a weekend in October 1967. This photo shows them at the harbor in Malmö, on their way home after staying with the spiritual leader in Falsterbo Castle, south of the city. You can see young journalist Lena Rosendahl talking to George. She d spent the weekend trying to make contact with them and she got her chance at the very last minute, just moments before they stepped on the ferry to Copenhagen Airport. I hadn't thought about what to ask, I was just concentrating on catching up with them, she later told Sydsvenskan newspaper. I managed to ask, what are you doing right now? meaning are you recording an album or something like that. George s reply was typically laconic. "We are trying to get on board a boat, he said before doing precisely that. At the time, it was assumed the Paul and George were visiting the Maharishi for a weekend of meditation, but Peter Brown (the Beatles long-time personal assistant) told a different story in his memoir. He claimed the Maharashi had been negotiating a television series with a US network and promising that the Beatles would appear on the show. Brown thus brought Paul and George to Falsterbo to try and convince the Maharashi to stop using the Beatles for his own PR purposes.

Here s an excerpt from an article he wrote for the Kvällsposten newspaper: For a couple of years I lived in this community, and I remember the aromas. From the wonderfully sweaty changing rooms in Heleneholm and Sorgenfri, to the smell of empty beer bottles in the dark club rooms on Palmgatan, via that sulphur smell, when "Russin" missed a shot at the pool table. And then the finest scent of all when you came out of the clubhouse on a sunny early summer day and the whole of Sofielund smelled of lilacs and roast veal. Palmgatan 6 had Malmö's last remaining outdoor toilet, which remained in use until 2006.

entries.summary: On 22nd March 1969, Judy Garland arrived in Malmö and checked in to the Savoy Hotel.
entries.description: On 22nd March 1969, Judy Garland arrived in Malmö and checked in to the Savoy Hotel. She wasn t in great shape, and it seemed unlikely that she d be physically able to perform her scheduled concert that evening at Kronprinsen's stage. Her gig in Gothenburg a few days earlier had been cancelled. However, local businessman Hugo åberg was determined that the show would go on and offered 90,000 kronor to ensure that the performance would take place. His tactics succeeded and Judy delivered a barnstorming show featuring her most-loved songs including Over the Rainbow . Tragically, it would be her penultimate show, and she died in London three months later from an overdose of sleeping pills. åberg was killed in a traffic accident in Malmö later that year.

entries.description: In 1964, Dan Walterström and Per Falck started a pop and rock club called Klubb Bongo. Its first home was the old Folkets Hus on Skolgatan, but by 1966 it had moved on to 18 Friisgatan. With concerts often organised together with the Malmö jazz club New Orleans, it quickly became a popular spot for young people with a passion for music and dancing. Dozens of Swedish and international stars have appeared here, perhaps most notably Jimi Hendrix on 23rd May 1967. It s a gig that s gone down in Malmö folklore. The audience loved it, but the local press hated it. The building was demolished in 1968. Photograph: Bilder i syd

He spent his days hanging round Möllevången, with a lively set of accomplices: stray dog Calle, fast-talking corner shop assistant Skogan, and, perhaps most memorably, his neighbour, played by Janne Malmsjö who drank too much and constantly talked about his bygone days on the football field (he went by the nickname Danskdödaren the Dane Killer). Nils Ahlroth, who played the main character, is in the centre of this photograph, with the series' creators Jacques Werup, åke Wihlney, Håkan Ersgård and Frank Andersson. entries.description: Gunnar "Siljabloo" Nilson (1925-1989) was one of Sweden's greatest jazz performers. The nickname came from a hit song the singer and clarinet player wrote in 1953. He was also known for his scat singing. For a period of his life he suffered with a severe alcohol problem, and by the early 1970s he was living ill and forgotten in an apartment here, Kristianstadsgatan 17. He later became sober and made a successful comeback. Siljabloo's life formed the basis of Jacques Werup s 2001 novel "Lev länge dö ung (Live Long Die Young). entries.name: När något går sönder...
entries.summary: När kyrkan revs . jag är egentligen inte särskilt religiös, gick bara förbi här när det hände.
entries.description: När kyrkan revs . jag är egentligen inte särskilt religiös, gick bara förbi här när det hände. Så här såg det ut. Något som gick sönder, kan inte förklara det bättre. Närmaste jag varit med om var när jag var 5-6 år. Pianot spändes på släpet, det var mammas piano, pappa körde. Jag satt i framsätet, utan bilbälte. När vi kom till soptippen först när pappa fick hjälp av sopgubbarna för att ösa ner pianot, först då förstod jag att det skulle gå sönder. Totalt. Och det gjorde det. Metall mot trä som krossades. Pappa, så uppfylld att ösa det över kanten, att få ner det till soptippen från släpkärran över tipprampen. Tårarna rann. Och rann. Jag bara grät och grät och fick ur mig: Piiiianooot. Pappa kom av sig, stannade upp efter det enorma braket när pianot landade på soptippen, och han tittade upp på mig, lite förvånad. Det var trasigt, helt sönder, det gick inte att spela på och det gick inte att laga . Men det var fint . grät jag. Jo, ja .det var fint .Men vi ska köpa ett nytt ett som vi kan spela på . Pappa såg också lite ledsen ut över spillrorna därnere, pianot var fint och nu var det helt massakrerat, krossat, dödat. Och nu kan vi åka och köpa en glass till dig . Den känslan, det var den känslan som sköljde över mig. När något går sönder. Kanske i onödan. Och ingen återvändo finns. Att inte kunna ångra sig. Varför skulle kyrkan rivas, den var ju hel, fungerande, och den liksom blickade mot staden . när man kom i parken och passerade träden så såg man kyrkan. Ett smycke på något sätt. Jag förstår att förändring behövs men, hur minns vi kyrkan hur kommer vi att minnas den? När jag går förbi det nybyggda bostadsområdet så tänker jag att kyrkan ligger där också samtidigt. Både och på samma gång. Och vad fanns på platsen innan kyrkan? Jag vet inte, men jag blir nyfiken.

entries.name: Eva Remeaus, ants and elephants
entries.summary: In the 1970s, Eva Remeaus (1950 1993) lived at Föreningsgatan 57.
entries.description: In the 1970s, Eva Remeaus (1950 1993) lived at Föreningsgatan 57. The much-loved actress is possibly best remembered for her musical performance in "Sven Klang's Quintet", first on-stage then on film (the film has been voted one of the best 25 Swedish films of all-time.) Her other on-stage musical roles include Polly Peachum in The Threepenny Opera and Sally Bowles in Cabaret, and she was a significant figure in both the Oktober musical theatre group and Tältprojektet ( The Tent Project ). Tältprojektet was a musical theater performance that toured Sweden in 1977. Held in a huge circus tent, it told the history of the Swedish working class and played to over 100,000 people over just one summer. Eva first found fame singing and acting in the cult TV series Fem myror är fler än fyra elefanter ( Five ants are more than four elephants ) where she both sang and acted. In 2006, it was named best Swedish children's program of all time by Folktoppen.

entries.description: One weekend in June 1965, there was a notorious party at Ola and Ingela Ström s parents place (Fersens Väg 4, to be precise). The Rolling Stones were at the center of it. They stayed at the apartment for a couple of nights around the time of their gig at Baltiska Hallen, and the siblings invited along some friends and local musicians. It turned into quite the event, and footage of the party later appeared alongside interviews with the band in Magnus Gertten and Stefan Berg's documentary film "Rolling like a Stone". Ola s band, The Gonks, practised at a rehearsal space on Västergatan and the Stones also popped in there during their stay in the city.

entries.summary: The Claes in Claesgatan is Claes Nestor Siegbahn.
entries.description: The Claes in Claesgatan is Claes Nestor Siegbahn. He was a bookkeeper who owned land in the Abel, Blenda, Christoffer, and Daniel neighbourhoods (i.e. the areas that Claesgatan runs through). He was friends with both Otto Fredrik Frick and Bengt Göran Ahlman they also give their names to streets around here. In 1971, the buildings here were threatened with demolition, prompting the residents to protest against what they called the "demolition mafia" (rivningsmaffian). The poster reads: "Every human being has the right to live where he thrives. We, at Claesgatan 5, are also human beings. We do not want to move to a sterile Rosengård atmosphere. We thrive here. Stop the demolition mafia!" Photograph: Bilder i Syd

entries.name: Club Max - RFSL
entries.summary: RFSL Malmö the Malmö chapter of what is now called The Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Rights was formed In 1971.
entries.description: RFSL Malmö the Malmö chapter of what is now called The Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Rights was formed In 1971. One of their earliest activities was to rent the restaurant here to host their nightclub Club Max. RFSL Malmö contained smaller factions, like the Gay Power Group, who carried out actions like "same-sex dancing" at the Kronprinsen restaurant. They also organized the city's first liberation demonstration. RFSL Malmö would later move into a space here, at östra Farmarvägen 21c. Their premises included "a lounge, a colour TV room, a discoth que room and an office". Some saw RFSL as a bourgeois organisation, and wanted to take a more radical approach to LGBTQI rights. This attitude brought about activist groups like Lila Faran, the 5-May group and HAML. They held demonstrations, distributed leaflets, gave out information to schools, and provided informal counselling. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text adapted from: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: The attack on Gay House
entries.summary: Gay House was founded by Lars Hector in 1971.
entries.description: Gay House was founded by Lars Hector in 1971. A gay club, it had a large visible sign outside, which was brave for the time. It was well attended, with singer/artist/local-legend Merry Lou often behind the bar. However, it was regularly targeted by homophobic pickpockets, and attacks by local thugs intensified on Good Friday 1978. The club was stormed several times, and homophobes smashed up the interior and poured petrol on the floors. The police arrived, but couldn t prevent the building being set alight. Gay House never reopened. Foto: Lars Hector Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: The first liberation marches
entries.summary: When the police raided the Stonewall Inn (one of the busiest gay bars in New York) in June 1969, it triggered spontaneous demonstrations, police violence, and a
entries.description: When the police raided the Stonewall Inn (one of the busiest gay bars in New York) in June 1969, it triggered spontaneous demonstrations, police violence, and all-out rioting that lasted several days. The following year, the Gay Liberation Parade was held to commemorate the event. These events became an inspiration for homosexual liberation across the world. In May 1971, the Gay Power Club in örebro held Sweden's first such demonstration. In autumn the same year, the newly formed RFSL Malmö (The Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Rights) initiated a demonstration with about 40 people marching from Club Max on östra Förstadsgatan to Stortorget, carrying placards with slogans like: "I am gay and proud", "We are the ones your mothers warned you about" and "Sexual equality".

entries.name: Cornelis Vreeswijk’s long Malmö history
entries.summary: Dutch-Swedish singer, songwriter, actor and poet Cornelis Vreeswijk lived in Malmö for several spells throughout his eventful life.
entries.description: Dutch-Swedish singer, songwriter, actor and poet Cornelis Vreeswijk lived in Malmö for several spells throughout his eventful life. He was here in 1968 and 1969, for example, when he took the lead role of Tevje in Malmö City Theater's production of "Fiddler on the Roof". But it was 1971 when Vreeswijk really made a permanent imprint on the city s consciousness. That year he put on a well-remembered floor show at Kronprinsen and then became one of the highlights of the city s first Folkfesten, held at Slottsparken. The cultural impact of American festivals like Monterey Pop and Woodstock had been felt in Sweden and had prompted the Festen på Gärdet event in Stockholm in 1970. Folkfesten was Malmö s equivalent, and Vreeswijk produced the most enduring memory with his version of John Lennon s "Power to the people", reworded as Slottsparken ät folket" (that is, Slottsparken for the people ). He also found time to release, "Spring mot Ulla - spring! Cornelis sings Bellman". One of his most popular records, it s a collection of unconventional recitals of Carl Michael Bellman ballads. Bellman was, of course, the key figure in Sweden s ballad tradition, a tradition that Vreeswijk resurrected in the second half of the twentieth century, while imbuing it with social and political relevance. The photograph on the cover is taken outside St Peters Church (S:t Petri kyrka) in Malmö.

entries.name: Light my Fire
entries.summary: Activist Agneta Berndt lived in this building when she was 18.
entries.description: Activist Agneta Berndt lived in this building when she was 18. In 1972, she wrote to the progressive Danish pair Inge and Sten who wrote a sex advice column for a Swedish newspaper to ask if there were any gay meeting places in Malmö. Two years later, Berndt sent a contact ad to the newspaper Kvällsposten, which was rejected on the grounds that it was a provocative sex contact . The ad read: 20-year-old dyke = gay = lesbian girl who likes jeans and sweaters, nice music and nature. Would like to meet you, a girl who is not afraid to show her true self to her surroundings. You enjoy doing things for other smiles . The ad was signed "Light my fire". At the time, Berndt was a member of the group that would become the Lesbisk Front in Malmö. entries.name: Marlene Dietrich at Malmö Stadsteater
entries.summary: The German-born actress and singer Marlene Dietrich (1901-1992) is famous for films like 1930 s The Blue Angel (in which she kissed a woman on the mouth) and so
entries.description: The German-born actress and singer Marlene Dietrich (1901-1992) is famous for films like 1930 s The Blue Angel (in which she kissed a woman on the mouth) and songs including Lili Marlene. She also renounced her German citizenship in 1939, becoming a US citizen and performing countless times for Allied troops during World War II. Post-war, she stayed in the US and lived an extravagant amorous life, loving both women and men. Some of her female partners were Mercedes de Acosta and Sweden s own Greta Garbo. On October 22, 1973, Marlene Dietrich performed two concerts at Malmö Stadsteater. The second show in paticular has passed into legend the cheering audience didn t want to go home! entries.name: ABF
entries.summary: ABF bildades för över 100 år sedan, den 16 november 1912.
entries.description: ABF bildades för över 100 år sedan, den 16 november 1912. Bakom grundandet stod Socialdemokraterna, LO och Kooperativa Förbundet. Tanken var att samordna och utveckla den bildningsverksamhet som redan pågick inom arbetarrörelsen. ABF Malmö har inte alltid huserat på Spånehusvägen 47. Tidigare höll studieförbundet till i Happachska villan som stod vid korsningen Bergsgatan/Friisgatan, på den tomt där tidningen Arbetet senare byggde sitt hus, och där Stadsarkivet idag ligger. 1938 flyttade ABF Malmö hit till Spånehusvägen 47, där de verkat sedan dess. På väggarna finns muralmålningar av Nils Wedel, Gunnar Nordborg, Gunnar Jonn och Bertil Landelius. De finns ännu kvar, gå gärna in och titta! Foto Stadsarkivet

entries.name: "Badtåget"
entries.summary: The Heleneholmsstigen cycle path follows the former railway line between Malmö and Trelleborg that opened in 1886.
entries.description: The Heleneholmsstigen cycle path follows the former railway line between Malmö and Trelleborg that opened in 1886. A branch line was added in 1904, linking Vellinge to Skanör and Falsterbo. Officially known as the Falsterbo line, it soon picked up the nickname Badtåget (bathing train), because it served so many swimmers heading to the coast. On Sundays during the summer season, an additional steam train puffed all the way to beaches at Näset. The Södervärn-Falsterbo section was closed down on 22 August 1971. "Heleneholmsstigen" is also the name of a short animated film by the filmmaker Henrik Möller, set right here. Check it out on YouTube!

entries.name: Betelkyrkan
entries.summary: Betelförsamlingen, eller som den först kallades, Evangeliska Missionsföreningen, bildades i Malmö den 16 maj 1885.
entries.description: Betelförsamlingen, eller som den först kallades, Evangeliska Missionsföreningen, bildades i Malmö den 16 maj 1885. Bildandet föregicks av en schism inom Evangeliska Lutherska Missionssällskapet. Nelly Hall hade under en tid predikat i denna församling i Malmö men protester uppkom då hon var kvinna vilket enligt många inte var förenligt med predikoutövande. Industrimannen Rudolf Fredrik Berg, som var aktiv i föreningen, ville medla, men vid omröstning föll hans förslag. Han och 120 andra medlemmar ur Missionsföreningen bröt sig då ut och bildade den nya församlingen med predikanten P.E. Dalqvist som föreståndare. Den 13 mars 1886 inköpte några medlemmar en tomt vid Kaptensgatan i Malmö och bildade A.B. Betel vilket företag uppförde en kyrka på tomten. Ordförande i aktiebolaget var Rudolf Fredrik Berg. Grundstenen lades den 30 juli 1886 i samband med ett stort bönemöte på platsen klockan 5 på morgonen. Kyrkan uppfördes i nyromansk stil efter ritningar av arkitekten John Smedberg och invigdes den 30 januari 1887. Den revs 1975 efter att församlingen hade flyttat sin verksamhet till den då nybyggda Stadionkyrkan.

entries.description: I Grynbodgatan startade en gång de tre schweiziska bröderna Bernhard, Nutin och Christoph Cloettas chokladfabrik som 1901 flyttade till Ljungsbro i östergötland. Innan dess hann de vara med på Stockholmsutställningen 1897 med en stor staty av kungaparet Oscar II och Sophia av Nassau i massiv choklad. Vikt: 600 kilo! Här i Grynbodarne, som var det gamla namnet på gatan, startade också något värre, dvs pestepidemin 1712 som skördade 65% av Malmöbornas liv på tre månader. Men i modern tid fanns här också danspalatset Baldakinen där många har lagt en sula i parketten. Foto: Stadsarkivet

Tillsammans med sin hustru Maj Sjöwall, också hon journalist, skrev han under författarnamnet SjöwallWahlöö dekalogen Roman om ett brott . Mellan 1965 och 1975 kom de tio böckerna där poliskommissarien Martin Beck är antihjälte och som uppmärksammades för sin fräna samhällskritik. Per Wahlöö ligger begravd i minneslunden.

entries.name: Amalthea sets sail
entries.summary: The Amalthea record company was started in 1977 by, among others, the musician Dan Hylander.
entries.description: The Amalthea record company was started in 1977 by, among others, the musician Dan Hylander. It was originally based at Ystadsgatan 22, before moving to Hamngatan 4 in 1984. The company was named after the ship of the same name that was blown up by young socialist activists in Malmö harbor in 1908. In its early years, it specialized in prog-rock but later broadened its range, and released records by Hylander, Mikael Wiehe, Nationalteatern, Grus i dojjan, Husmother's Breast and Petula and the Clarks. The photo shows a 21-year-old Niels Jensen, who had just released his third album "Celluloid" in 1985. In 1993, Amalthea was purchased by MNW, a record company then based in Vaxholm, near Stockholm.

entries.name: Tintomara - Fyran (1978–2002)
entries.summary: Beyond the whitewashed gates and up the stairs, you could find Tintomara, which opened in 1978.
entries.description: Beyond the whitewashed gates and up the stairs, you could find Tintomara, which opened in 1978. It was a members-only club with a bell at the door. The venue had previously housed the porn cinema Venus, so the interior was dominated by red velvet. The name Tintomara was borrowed from the androgynous character loved by both men and women in C.J.L. Almqvist's 1834 novel The Queen's Diadem ( Drottningens juvelsmycke ). The club was later modernized and renamed Fyran. For decades, the club served as a breathing space for the queer community, offering drag shows and dancefloors. Like Gay House, the club was subjected to homophobic attacks including Molotov cocktails thrown into the entrance. Foto: Bilder i Syd samt Illustration: målning, kolteckning, vaxkrita, Snapperupsgatan 8-10-12 av Larsson, åke Waldemar (1913-1995) - 1995 - Malmö museer, Sweden - CC BY-NC-ND. https://www.europeana.eu/sv/item/91658/MM_objekt_231860 Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Blondie leave their hammer at home
entries.summary: On the 18 February 1978, American new wave band Blondie played at Dad s Dancehall on Föreningsgatan 54.
entries.description: On the 18 February 1978, American new wave band Blondie played at Dad s Dancehall on Föreningsgatan 54. Fronted by charismatic singer Debbie Harry wearing her trademark thigh-high boots they powered through 24 songs at a furious pace. It was a couple of months before the group really hit the big time with their Parallel Lines album, but they had already become cult favorites. The band stayed at the Hotel Scandinavia on the corner of östra Förstadsgatan and Drottninggatan, and popped into Ahlförs music shop in the same building. Alongside Olle Berggren, a journalist for local newspaper Kvällposten newspaper, they spent some time checking out Farfisa organs. The Italian-made electronic instruments were very popular with new wave bands of that period, and Blondie keyboardist Jimmy Destri was known to play his with a hammer on occasion.On the 18 February 1978, American new wave band Blondie played at Dad s Dancehall on Föreningsgatan 54. entries.name: Kvinnohusgruppen i Malmö
entries.summary: At the end of the 1970s, Kvinnohusgruppen (the Women s House Group) was formed in Malmö in a first-floor, three-room property in the west-end of the old city.
entries.description: At the end of the 1970s, Kvinnohusgruppen (the Women s House Group) was formed in Malmö in a first-floor, three-room property in the west-end of the old city. The group s members worked for women's rights in society. Through activities as diverse as political meetings and cabaret nights, they drew attention to a need that had been previously overlooked in Malmö a space that was open to all women, and which offered community and solidarity. Kvinnohusgruppen hosted study groups in subjects like photography, women's history and women's literature. Many of the participants were lesbians and the circumstances of gay women was always a central point of discussion. On March 8, 1985, a a benefit concert was held in support of Kvinnohusgruppen at Moriska Pavilion in Folkets Park. All the artists who performed were women and the majority were lesbians. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Malmö stad

entries.name: Secret meeting places
entries.summary: The city's parks have always been meeting places for men who have sex with men.
entries.description: The city's parks have always been meeting places for men who have sex with men. Stories have long circulated about handkerchiefs and scarves that, when folded or tied in particular ways, would signal requests or offers. In 1990, RFSL Rådgivningen ran a campaign for safer sex, filling birdhouses with condoms and lubricants in several of Malmö's parks. At the same time, "gay bashing" (violence against gays) was happening in many of the same parks. Violent crimes against homosexual men were common in Sweden during the first part of the 1990s, and the area around the Pegasus statue in Slottsparken was rumoured to be an especially dangerous place. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Malmö Gay Radio
entries.summary: Malmö Gay Radio began life in Ken Paine's wardrobe on Stenbocksgatan in 1980.
entries.description: Malmö Gay Radio began life in Ken Paine's wardrobe on Stenbocksgatan in 1980. However, since the transmitter had a range of only ten metres, they soon got out of the closet! They rented space in Radio MCB's premises, before getting their own specially built studio in RFSL's basement on Jöns Filsgatan 2 they later moved into the party rooms so that the studio could double up as a DJ booth. Ken was the licence holder, broadcast technician, carpenter, and interviewer of English speakers. Guests on the station included Shere Hite, Tom Robinson, and Divine the latter interviewed at a gig at KB in Malmö. A former chairwoman of RFSL Malmö says: Radio MGR is worth mentioning. We did a good job of making people feel less lonely. Some people would even take their car and drive out into the woods so they could listen without being detected." Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Ken Paine

entries.name: Ribersborgs kallbadhus
entries.summary: "Kallis", one of the city's nude saunas and bathing spots, has been an important and well-attended unofficial meeting place for LGBTQI people over the years.
entries.description: "Kallis", one of the city's nude saunas and bathing spots, has been an important and well-attended unofficial meeting place for LGBTQI people over the years. It was built in 1898, and had its own station on the railway between Malmö and Limhamn. A storm around Christmas 1902 more or less destroyed the bathhouse, causing it to be completely rebuilt. It has retained the same look since then. For more than a century it has been a place for swimming, sunbathing, and making contacts that have led to long-term relationships and shorter acquaintances. But woe betide anyone on the women s side of the bathhouse anyway who lies down in a place that has been set aside for one of the old regulars! Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Malmö stadsarkiv

entries.name: Möllevångsgården
entries.summary: I dessa byggnader har det varit allt från glashytta till gayklubb och kulturförening!
entries.description: I dessa byggnader har det varit allt från glashytta till gayklubb och kulturförening! Lokalerna byggdes av virke från ett rivet sågverk i Småland och invigdes samtidigt med Terrariet 1983. Två anställda glasblåsare skulle ge staden ett eget glasrike, men verksamheten var inte lönsam och lade ner redan två år senare. I stället blev det ungdomsverksamhet med caf och olika föreningar inom arbetarrörelsen använde huset. även RFSL arrangerade under en period fester och klubbar i byggnaden. Under en femtonårsperiod fanns här klubbar som Inkonst och Debaser som också arrangerade många livespelningar med såväl etablerade som nya artister. entries.name: Blåkulla Women's Collective
entries.summary: "Blåkulla" became emblematic of the many women's collectives around Möllevången and St Knuts Torg in the 1970s and 1980s.
entries.description: "Blåkulla" became emblematic of the many women's collectives around Möllevången and St Knuts Torg in the 1970s and 1980s. In this large four-room, third-floor apartment, lesbian women lived collectively for a number of years, socialising informally with like-minded people. In the absence of public spaces where they could meet freely, lesbian women often hung out in private homes, Blåkulla also became a place where study groups and feminist activists would meet. Large parties with live music and dancing were also common, and helped create networks and opportunities for socialising for young gay people invited into the community. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Malmö stadsarkiv

entries.name: Restaurang Zorba
entries.summary: Now the location of Tusen&2 restaurant, this corner was home to the Zorba restaurant throughout the 1980s.
entries.description: Now the location of Tusen&2 restaurant, this corner was home to the Zorba restaurant throughout the 1980s. It was a cozy place that served simple Greek food and drinks, and quickly became an unofficial gay meeting place. Gay men and women would meet in a relaxed environment over a plate of food and a beer in the early evenings. As the chairs at the tables became occupied, new guests would pick up stools from behind the jukebox, and the room would often fill up, especially at the weekend. The restaurant changed owners in the early 1990s. It was renovated and the gay-friendly character disappeared. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Malmö stadsarkiv

entries.name: Stora Kvarngatan 28
entries.summary: Kvarnen i namnet syftar på stubbamöllan Vallamöllan.
entries.description: Kvarnen i namnet syftar på stubbamöllan Vallamöllan. Väderkvarnen fanns redan på den tid då Kalmarbastionen låg på platsen och när denna revs ner och schaktades bort fick kvarnen finnas kvar, då på en höjd som kallades Möllebacken och som givit namn åt dagens kvarter. Själva möllan revs 1853. På Stora Kvarngatan 28, det tredje huset från vänster i bilden, bodde i mitten av 1980-talet tonårsidolen Freddie Hansson, känd från gruppen Noice som var en av landets största musikaliska akter under några år. De gamla husen revs i början av 90-talet och Riksbyggen byggde det nya fyravåningshuset som en gång när den sortens media konsumerades flitigt inrymde Kvarn Video. Foto: Bilder i syd

entries.name: Fredman: A Malmö institution
entries.summary: For many years, the legendary Malmö nightclub Fredman stood at Regementsgatan 4.
entries.description: For many years, the legendary Malmö nightclub Fredman stood at Regementsgatan 4. It hosted countless memorable events, including "Cabaret Fredagsbarnen" from 1970 onward it was a chaotic blend of music, theater, improvisation, poetry, politics and comedy, organized by Jacques Werup, Lasse Söderberg and Rolf Sersam. In 1985 Wilmer X recorded his live album V-I-L-D here, and in 1988 Chet Baker came to visit. Over the years it became home to an evolving set of musical genres and movements, and it was a longtime hub for the city s punk scene. In this photograph, Malmö musicians Jan-Eric "Fjellis" Fjellström, Arne Franck, Mikael Wiehe and Håkan Nyberg stand outside the club. Fredman was referenced in "Bluesen i Malmö", a 2017 song by celebrated Swedish singer Thåström (formerly of Ebba Grön and Imperiet): "I see Leman, Maersk, Hamburg S d rolling by I see Kinakrogen and the ghetto the first time I came here I see Fredman's and cheap beer at Sjöfartshotellet Back and forth across the bridge, back and forth

entries.name: The Pogues’ fairytales of New York and Malmö
entries.summary: Kulturbolaget - then located here in Erikslust - held a unique Pogues gig on 6th November 1985 unique in that singer Shane MacGowan was absent and replaced for
entries.description: Kulturbolaget - then located here in Erikslust - held a unique Pogues gig on 6th November 1985 unique in that singer Shane MacGowan was absent and replaced for one night only by Elvis Costello. MacGowan wasn t at the show but he was in town, and busy making an enduring contribution to musical history. MacGowan was unavailable because he had been laid low by double pneumonia. That wasn t enough to contain his creativity though, and he spent the evening in a feverish state finalizing the lyrics to one of the greatest ever Christmas records, Fairytale of New York. The illness seemed to bring an extra dimension to the song. You get a lot of delirium and stuff, he later told the BBC, and I got a lot of good images out of that. Reports vary about whether he spent the evening in a hotel or a hospital, but next time you hear the line in the second verse, lying there almost dead on a drip in your bed, you can be pretty sure the bed in question was somewhere in these parts.
