entries.name: Salong Caluff ́s
entries.summary: Caluff s Salon opened in 1987.
entries.description: Caluff s Salon opened in 1987. Founder Jens Hallberg, himself gay, describes how it came about: I made some attempts to apply for jobs at salons in Malmö, and was disappointed at how timid and uniform everything was. I had a trial at one place they thought I did a great job, but said that I didn t fit in there. They thought I was deviating from their style, and that I was probably going out to completely different places than they were. (Yes, I went to much gayer places!). I thought that kind of environment would be intolerable, so I knew that I would have to open my own place, where we d cut and style hair the way that the customers actually wanted them, instead of doing what was being dictated by daft fashion trends. I wanted to work with styles that were really cool, and thought it was important that the salon could be a meeting place too. The 20-year-old version of me was extremely confident about what was actually cool, and I was pretty uninterested in putting labels on things. I was so happy about the diversity of what became my clientele, and also about having the opportunity to style hair in a way that would make other hairdressers turn away in disgust! Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Jens Hallberg

entries.name: The park outside 4:an
entries.summary: Sadly, threats and violence have been part of Malmö's LGBTQI history, affecting the lives of many LGBTQI people.
entries.description: Sadly, threats and violence have been part of Malmö's LGBTQI history, affecting the lives of many LGBTQI people. A former chairman of RFSL Malmö remembers how the association took action against homophobic attacks, back in the 1980s: I remember that the board asked the police to come to our premises for talks. A couple of guys had been assaulted on their way home from the 4:an nightclub. The police came up with the idea of setting a trap. We got some volunteers to stand outside 4:an on a Saturday night. I saw some guys came over and start being very threatening. Suddenly police cars came from all directions and the boys ran across the park. They were picked up by the police and eventually went to trial. As far as I remember, the harassment stopped after that. " Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Bilder i syd

entries.name: World AIDS Day
entries.summary: The first World AIDS Day was held on December 1 1988 and was dedicated to the fight against AIDS.
entries.description: The first World AIDS Day was held on December 1 1988 and was dedicated to the fight against AIDS. The following year, RFSL Malmö (The Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Rights) distributed 10,000 condoms on this day: We started at 8.00 by driving around Malmö's larger car parks, and putting a small package on every windscreen. Between 15.00 and 18.00, we stood in the corner of Södra Förstadsgatan and Friisgatan, handing out mulled wine, gingerbread, information, and condoms. In the evening we had an open house on Korsgatan, and a condom giveaway at Rosengård sports hall, where the band So What also played. The evening's events finished at 23.30, capping off a very successful day . Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Olof Palmes staty
entries.summary: Olof Palme (1927 - 1986) was a Social Democrat politician and two-time Prime Minister of Sweden (1969 - 76 and 1982 - 86) who was assassinated on a Stockholm st
entries.description: Olof Palme (1927 - 1986) was a Social Democrat politician and two-time Prime Minister of Sweden (1969 - 76 and 1982 - 86) who was assassinated on a Stockholm street on 28 February 1986. This statue was erected three years later. It was made by sculptor Willy Gordon who grew up in Malmö, and who made several other statues of figures from the labour movement. Olof Palme visited Folkets park on many occasions mostly to meet colleagues, though he also gave speeches at the May Day celebrations in 1966, 1969 and 1980. The statue is made of bronze and granite, and was donated by the National Folkets Park Organisation.

entries.name: The Leathermen
entries.summary: SLM Malmö (Scandinavian Leather Men) came together in a private apartment in 1989.
entries.description: SLM Malmö (Scandinavian Leather Men) came together in a private apartment in 1989. The association's purpose was to: "promote and facilitate social contacts for gay and bisexual men who are interested in and dress in leather, rubber, western, uniform and the like". The club's first emblem was a griffin s head wearing a leather cap. The griffin s head is prominent on Malmö's coat of arms. The club s dress code was jeans and leather. At one time, SLM Malmö had their premises at Ystadsgatan 13. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: Noaks Ark and Positiva Gruppen
entries.summary: In the early 1980s, the first reports of AIDS emerged.
entries.description: In the early 1980s, the first reports of AIDS emerged. The disease was labelled the "gay plague" because it was associated with male homosexuality. Voluntary organizations were formed to help HIV-positive and AIDS patients. Here on Baltzarsgatan in 1987, Noaks Ark set up its first premises. An informal organisation, Positiva Gruppen, developed here too, when "18 HIV-positive boys met and ate pea soup with punch". In 1989, Positiva Gruppen (PG-Syd) moved to Södergatan and became an official association. Per-Olof Persson, or Peo as he was known, served as chairman from 1989 to 1993, and made an especially significant impact through his hard work and personality. He died in 1995 at just 33 years old, but his life and influence is commemorated in a scholarship that continues to be awarded annully. The stigma and trauma around AIDS in Sweden is perhaps most memorably described in Jonas Gardell's novel trilogy Torka aldrig tårar utan handskar (Don t Ever Wipe Tears without Gloves). Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text adapted from: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Bob Dylan
entries.summary: även en av världens mest kända artister kan gå vilse.
entries.description: även en av världens mest kända artister kan gå vilse. Så gjorde också Bob Dylan i Malmö i maj 1989, inte alls långt från hotellet där han den gången bodde. Turligt nog stötte han på ett par som välvilligt hjälpte honom tillbaka. Som tack fick de biljetter till den blivande Nobelpristagarens spelning på Christinehofs slott. Vid en annan av Dylans flera besök i Malmö, i oktober 2015, flanerade han tillsammans med en väninna på Engelbrektsgatan och gick in på Miva Fine Art Gallery. Ett galleri som just då ställde ut konst av - Bob Dylan!

entries.name: RFSL, Korsgatan
entries.summary: When RFSL (the Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Rights) moved from Eden, they found a new location on Korsgatan in eastern Malmö.
entries.description: When RFSL (the Swedish Federation for Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Transgender, Queer and Intersex Rights) moved from Eden, they found a new location on Korsgatan in eastern Malmö. The association's then treasurer Eva Törnegren remembers: One evening, the cabaret group Sinkadus played a show there. When it was over, a group were standing outside talking. There was absolutely no loud music, but the neighbours still complained about the noise. With that in mind, we didn t dare to renovate the place. We had the space for about a year and had meetings there, but we could never have parties. We had to break the contract, and that was followed by a very difficult period where we didn t have any premises. We had to rent space at different restaurants in the city for a while. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto: Malmö stadsarkiv

entries.name: Skönhet kommer
entries.summary: Queer people and attitudes were at the forefront of the Malmö club scene in the early 1990s.
entries.description: Queer people and attitudes were at the forefront of the Malmö club scene in the early 1990s. Skönhet kommer (Beauty is Coming) was one of the outcomes. The organizers were searching for a venue for their artistic activities, and ended up in an abandoned industrial building. With this location, their plans changed to hosting an underground club with party nights, which in itself became an artistic project. They held conceptual parties with different themes, with the premises being remodelled for every event. Themes included, for example, the French Revolution. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira förlag Foto 1. Jens Hallberg Foto 2. Poster. Marie Olsson

entries.name: Herta Wirén 1899-1991
entries.summary: I minneslunden vilar författaren Herta Wir n.
entries.description: I minneslunden vilar författaren Herta Wir n. Hon växte upp på Möllevången och har skildrat arbetarstadsdelen från 1900-talets början. Herta debuterade 1975 med uppväxtromanen En bit bröd med Anna . 1906 flyttade hennes familj in i det nybyggda huset vid Möllevångstorget 3. Så här beskrev hon den ofattbara lyxen. Lägenheten var ljus med ett stort rum, hade ett bra kök med fönster åt gården, en stor järnvask, en glänsande svart spis med bakugn, en rymlig garderob och en väl tilltagen tambur. Dessutom fanns en kakelugn med mässingsluckor. Litteratur och att skriva var hennes största intressen, ibland läste hon i skenet från gaslyktorna från Möllevångstorget utanför. På 1930-talet blev hon den första kvinnan i Malmö skolstyrelse och på hennes agenda fanns kamp för fri skolmat och fria skolböcker. Efter debuten följde sju romaner på elva år och som 90-åring fick hon Malmö Stads kulturpris. Foto: Bilder i syd
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Fredrik Roos 1951-1991
entries.summary: Fredrik Roos hade utbildat sig på Handelshögskolan och kom från ekonomiskt goda förhållanden.
entries.description: Fredrik Roos hade utbildat sig på Handelshögskolan och kom från ekonomiskt goda förhållanden. Familjen ägde bland annat Skånska Banken där fadern Axel var vd. Fredrik samlade konst med stor passion, en god affär var köpet av Nils von Dardels Den döende dandyn för 3,2 miljoner kronor 1984. Fyra år senare sålde han den vidare för 13 miljoner. 1988 grundade Roos konstmuseet Rooseum i det gamla elverket som numera är Moderna Museet och här hängdes nu även hans egen storslagna konstsamling med nordisk samtidskonst. Som homosexuell tvingades han leva ett dubbelliv. Fredrik Roos var en av de som dog av sjukdomen AIDS.

entries.name: Jerry Williams starts his own Heartbreak Hotel
entries.summary: From the early sixties all the way into the twenty-first century, Jerry Williams was Sweden's king of rock and roll.
entries.description: From the early sixties all the way into the twenty-first century, Jerry Williams was Sweden's king of rock and roll. He first came to public attention as the lead singer of The Violents. They were part of a wave of Swedish bands influenced by American rock-and-roll and British beat music. They certainly learned from the best they supported Little Richard in 1962 and the Beatles in 1963. Williams had a hugely successful solo career in Sweden and by 1991 he had reached living legend status he even appeared on a stamp! He was co-owner of a chain of rock-themed bars and restaurants across Sweden, including the Heartbreak Hotel on Södergatan 16 which opened in November of that year. Jerry was on hand on opening night to pour beers, mingle with guests and play an exclusive concert.

entries.name: Eurovision’s first trip to Malmö
entries.summary: Malmö first hosted the Eurovision Song Contest in 1992 at the city s ice stadium (Isstadion).
entries.description: Malmö first hosted the Eurovision Song Contest in 1992 at the city s ice stadium (Isstadion). Sweden was represented by Christer Björkman who sang "I morgon är en annan dag" ("Tomorrow is another day") and came second last. The winner was Linda Martin, taking the first of three consecutive Irish victories. The winning song, " Why me ?", was written by Jonny Logan. It was his third victory, since he had won as a singer in 1980 ("What's Another Year") and 1987 ("Hold me now", which he also wrote). It was second time lucky for Linda: she was runner-up in 1984, behind Sweden s winning entry, "Diggiloo Diggiley" by Herreys.

entries.name: The fight for registered partnerships
entries.summary: On this street corner in 1993, members of RFSL and the RFSU, along with pastor Christer Kyr us, collected signatures for The Registered Partnerships Bill that w
entries.description: On this street corner in 1993, members of RFSL and the RFSU, along with pastor Christer Kyr us, collected signatures for The Registered Partnerships Bill that would go on to be an important stepping stone in promoting equality for gay people. They were opposed by members of the Livets Ord church, who stood closeby singing. The contrast could not be greater. The Registered Partnership Act passed into law in 1995. entries.name: The Cardigans move in
entries.summary: Den 1 juli 1994 flyttade medlemmarna i pop- och rockgruppen The Cardigans in på Södra Förstadsgatan 68 när de lämnade Jönköping för Malmö.
entries.description: Den 1 juli 1994 flyttade medlemmarna i pop- och rockgruppen The Cardigans in på Södra Förstadsgatan 68 när de lämnade Jönköping för Malmö. Lägenheten på 170 kvadratmeter utgjorde kollektiv för Bengt Lagerberg som spelade trummor, Lasse Johansson på keyboard, Nina Persson som sjöng, Magnus Sveningsson som spelade bas och Peter Svensson som var gitarrist. Gruppen bodde i lägenheten i 1,5 år. The Cardigans fick en stor internationell karriär, har fått flera Grammis- och Rockbjörnspriser och är invalda i Swedish Music Hall of Fame. Gruppen är fortfarande verksam, men Peter Svensson turnerar inte längre med bandet utan har ersatts av Oskar Humlebo.

entries.name: Regnbågsfestival - Malmö Pride
entries.summary: Malmö s first Regnbågsfestival was held in 1995.
entries.description: Malmö s first Regnbågsfestival was held in 1995. It featured theatre, lectures, art, music, worship, and celebration. The first Rainbow Parade followed in 1996, marching from Snapperupsgatan to St Knuts Torg. About 200 people participated. In 2015, the festival changed its name to Malmö Pride, and in 2019 around 15,000 people marched in the Pride Parade from Stortorget to Folkets Park. Foto: Malmö Stadsarkiv Text: A Ride to Pride en kartguide till Malmös hbtqi-historia, Malmö Stadsarkiv

entries.name: From the Triangle and the Opera to Europe!
entries.summary: When Jan Johansen came to Malmö in the spring of 1995 it was not only to hit the shops at the Triangeln shopping mall.
entries.description: When Jan Johansen came to Malmö in the spring of 1995 it was not only to hit the shops at the Triangeln shopping mall. He was in town to compete in Melodifestivalen, the event that decides Sweden s entry to Eurovision, with the smooth ballad Se på mig. The song had been coauthored by Ingela Pling Forsman, one of Swedens most prominent songwriters. No less than 40 of her songs have competed in Melodifestivalen, and when Jan Johansson sang Se på mig she had already won the contest with one of the most loved bangers to come out of Sweden in the 80 s - Bra vibrationer- sang by Kicki Danielsson in 1985. This year was once again her year - Jan Johansen scored 64 points from the Malmö Opera stage - enough to win the competition. Except for Johansen, four other winers of Mello have been selected at the Malmö Opera. In 1988 Tommy Körberg won with Stad i ljus Although it only managed twelfth place at Eurovision in Dublin, this song has remained extremely popular in Sweden and is now in the Church of Sweden s official hymnbook. In 1991 Carola won with Fångad av en stormvind . This was Carola s second Melodifestivalen victory (she also won in Malmö in 1983) and this time she went all the way, winning Eurovision in Rome later that year. In 1998 Jill Johnsson won with "Kärleken är". To date, this is the last Swedish Eurovision song with lyrics in Swedish - which were also written by Ingela Pling Forsman. In 2001 Friends won with "Listen to your heartbeat". Although somewhat overshadowed by accusations that it plagiarized Belgium s 1996 Eurovision entry, the distance från the Opera stage to Eurovision was not long that year, as the Olsen Brothers had won the contest the preceding year with Fly on the wings of love. Hence Friends could simply cross the newly inaugurated öresund bridge and compete in Copenhagen - where they finished on fifth place. Click here to see Johansens 1995 entry!

entries.description: Entertainment and events organiser Lars Hector built, owned and operated Restaurang G, on Gustav Adolfs Torg. It was an openly gay place that ran between 1998 and 2006. The interior was designed by his partner, architect Abelardo Gonzalez, and the exterior was designed by a Danish architect. Every Sunday it became a gay club. A lot of people came out! , says Lars. entries.summary: In the 1990s, readers of RFSL Malmö's member magazine, Traffic, were introduced to the Indigo Girls, "the proud football lesbians" who were tearing up the local
entries.description: In the 1990s, readers of RFSL Malmö's member magazine, Traffic, were introduced to the Indigo Girls, "the proud football lesbians" who were tearing up the local amateur football scene. (They actually played their games on the other side of Pildammsvägen, where the sports facilities have since been replaced by newly built houses). Malmö has also been home to Marta, the best female football player of all time. The Brazilian played for FC Rosengård from 2014 to 2017, before moving on to Orlando Pride in the USA. In 2021, she got engaged to teammate Toni Pressley. FC Rosengård is considered the most successful team in Swedish women's football. Foto 1. Malmö stadsarkiv Foto 2. entries.description: If you like house and techno, you shouldn t have missed Wonk! Between 2001 and 2018, it was a gay club night held first on Adelgatan, then later at the old city hall building on Amiralsgatan 20. Joakim Cederholm, who ran the club, oversaw over 900 Wonk parties before moving on to open the Red Shoe Bar on Drottninggatan with his partner Johan Carlsson. entries.name: On the beach with Franz Ferdinand
entries.summary: By summer 2003, Franz Ferdinand were getting some feverish attention from the British music press even though they had yet to release any records.
entries.description: By summer 2003, Franz Ferdinand were getting some feverish attention from the British music press even though they had yet to release any records. So, producer Tore Johansson brought the band to Malmö and to Gula Studion so that they could record their debut album away from the spotlight. They even slept in the studio, says Gula co-founder Jens Lindgård, who engineered the record. We moved some beds in, and they lived here all through the recording. That meant they could rehearse day and night, and I really think it helped them come together as a band. Although they worked long hours, the band still found time to sample the Malmö summer. The studio got hold of some bikes for them and suggested they cycle down for a swim at Ribersborg beach. Unfortunately, drummer Paul Thomson didn t know how to ride a bike, so singer Alex Kapranos patiently taught him. They eventually made it to Ribban and learned something else about their drummer: he couldn t swim either. Alex ended up being Paul s swimming instructor that day too. And the debut album? It won the Mercury Music Prize and sold over 3.6 million copies worldwide.

entries.description: Alldeles invid stora entr n finner vi ett glashus som trots att det är förhållandevis ungt ändå har en spännande historia. Ursprungligen låg huset på den stora bomässan Bo01 i Västra Hamnen där det väckte uppmärksamhet med sina åtta meter höga väggar. Då var det caf . 2004 blev byggnaden ett fjärilshus i Folkets Park där det var 88% luftfuktighet och ständigt 28 graders värme. I detta tropiska klimat fanns då 250 fjärilar av 30 olika arter. Något år senare blev det karibiska rytmer, mat och dryck i det som kallades Cuba Caf och där ett stort antal Malmöbor sedan dess lärt sig dansa salsa. entries.name: Tomboy
entries.summary: At the turn of the year 2004/2005, a hetero-friendly gay club opened in this building, which had previously been home to the Bodoni cafe (which was operated by
entries.description: At the turn of the year 2004/2005, a hetero-friendly gay club opened in this building, which had previously been home to the Bodoni cafe (which was operated by the Social Democrat newspaper Arbetet). It was an outward-looking, open club for a clientele that was generally unaccustomed to exposure. It was decided that admission would always be free, so that everyone who wanted to could afford to come. One of the founders, Marie Olsson, says: "We were doing something queer and everyone got to be part of our big queer family. A lot of local bands got a chance to play here, and the focus was punk, rock and electronic. It also became a bridge to the other clubs that were connected to Bodoni, and that created openness and incredible political explosiveness in the DIY spirit. It was a fantastic atmosphere and all kinds of people came there." Tomboy later moved to Moriskan, which brought them new and different visitors. Text: Jeanette Rosengren, Kira Förlag Foto: Malmö stadsarkiv

entries.name: Skanör City Hall
entries.summary: The city hall was finished in 1777.
entries.description: The city hall was finished in 1777. Not much has changed during the years, but the building has of course been renovated. The roof has been replaced, but with the same kind of beaver-tail bricks as the original. Leonard de la Rose was the mayor from 1752 up until his death in 1784. He was also a member of Parliament, combined Skanör and Falsterbo into one town, had the square set in stone, constituted a post office, amongst other things. This did not make him popular with the people in town. The vast majority wanted to abolish the city rights and get rid of the mayor and all of the work and costs he came with!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Falsterbo church
entries.summary: It is a big and spacious church.
entries.description: It is a big and spacious church. Built in the 14th century and of course annexed and renovated many times for nearly 700 years. During the 16th and 17th century both the church and town were completely flooded. The church was excavated several times, while the town was moved a couple hundred meters in from the shore. The rest of medieval Falsterbo still lies underneath the dunes. The church still has a few wooden sculptures from the chatolic times. Most impressive is Kristofferskåpet with a sculpture of St Kristoffer and paintings on the doors of his martyrdom.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skanör’s Church
entries.summary: A hundred years separate the pictures, but the church looks mostly the same.
entries.description: A hundred years separate the pictures, but the church looks mostly the same. It has looked almost the same for 600 years. The latest edition was the high altar. The church is originally from the 13th century. Some of the walls may be a bit older. The church has stood fast through wars, storms, fires, and floods. The four elements have not been particularly merciful towards Skanör, but the church has stood its ground in all types of weather.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A bygone Skanör
entries.summary: Skanör's square around 1870 seen from the clock tower of the church.
entries.description: Skanör's square around 1870 seen from the clock tower of the church. The city hall to the left and school to the right. Straight ahead behind the city hall the area that burned down in 1874 can be seen.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The old vicarage
entries.summary: The old vicarage burned to the ground in 1885 together with most of Skanör.
entries.description: The old vicarage burned to the ground in 1885 together with most of Skanör. The large lime-tree to the left is described by Linn on his trip through Skåne in 1749: Vicar Corvin had, outside his house, such a splendid, leaf and branch-filled lime-tree, that could be desired, and thereunder a small earth embankment, to pleasantly sit on beautiful summer eves.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Behind the City Hall (Rådhuset)
entries.summary: Rådhusgatan with Hammargården to the right and a part of the area that burned down in 1874 to the left.
entries.description: Rådhusgatan with Hammargården to the right and a part of the area that burned down in 1874 to the left. The picture was taken just before 1870, but was sold as a postcard 30 years later.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Mellangatan before the fires
entries.summary: Here we can see down Mellangatan with the church at its back.
entries.description: Here we can see down Mellangatan with the church at its back. The year is around 1870, before the big fires. All houses and farms in the picture burned down in 1885. The reason the fires could lay waste to such a large area can be seen in the picture. The houses leaned on each other, and when one house caught on fire the rest followed. A kind of domino effect.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Fire in the hole!
entries.summary: Falsterbo lighthouse stood finished in 1795.
entries.description: Falsterbo lighthouse stood finished in 1795. It was designed by Olof Tempelman and was placed further out on the isthmus than the old lighthouse placement on Kolabacken. As can be seen on picture 4, there was an open fire in the tower at first. Today, it is surrounded by the golf course and a verdant grove, but on the first picture it is free from both golf balls and trees. The picture is from 1873 and is the oldest known photo from Falsterbo.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: City gate and algae ditches
entries.summary: A city needs a wall, moat, or some other border to divide city and land.
entries.description: A city needs a wall, moat, or some other border to divide city and land. In Skanör and Falsterbo there was no stone and no timber. Instead, there were algae ditches. The word ditch comes from Dutch and means moat. During the years, the word has for some reason changed meaning, and it is now called algae moats . An algae moat consists of peat and algaes interspersed, not kelp algae since it rots, eelgrass is where it's at. There were 30 kilometers of algae moats on Falsterbonästet some time into the 1900s. Nowadays they are not maintained and have therefore collapsed.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skanör is rebuilt
entries.summary: östergatan seen from Rådhustorget in Skanör.
entries.description: östergatan seen from Rådhustorget in Skanör. First, a picture from around 1880. The area behind the city hall that burned down in 1874 is starting to be rebuilt. A patch of grass which was named "Rundningen" has been planted on the square. Only the priest's and mayor's families has a key to the gate!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A Skanör that disappeared
entries.summary: You are standing on the crossroad between östergatan and Kaptensgatan, looking north.
entries.description: You are standing on the crossroad between östergatan and Kaptensgatan, looking north. The first picture shows the houses that burned down in 1885 in the foreground. But the white gable belongs to a new house that was built after the fire in 1874 and survived the big fire in 1885. One can sense the city hall and the church behind it. A building can be glimpsed in the graveyard as well. It was Klockargården that was torn down in the 1890s. Next picture. You'll have to turn around completely to see östergatan to the south. None of these estates survived the fire of 1885. The last picture is of a woodcut from 1879. We see the same part of östergatan as in the last picture, but the artist has managed to draw a weird gable on the estate to the left.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The beach hotel
entries.summary: The hotel was built back in 1897.
entries.description: The hotel was built back in 1897. It was the first establishment that turned to tourists in Falsterbo. A hotel and restaurant with music and an unbeatable location, just 50 meters from the beach. This is where the first summer guests arrived. That was before they had made their own villas. However, in the 1960s, things went sideways. The hotel stood and decayed. The municipality bought the whole thing and tore it down in the middle of the 70s.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Traffic junction on Storgatan
entries.summary: The junction between Storgatan and Gamelgatan was a resting place for the stagecoach from Vellinge with a journey continuing to Malmö or further out into the world.
entries.description: The junction between Storgatan and Gamelgatan was a resting place for the stagecoach from Vellinge with a journey continuing to Malmö or further out into the world. In the house behind the stagecoach, on picture 2, the "warehouse" Wertheim was situated during its first years. A fire in 1911 led to the decision to invest in a new business building. The yellow house here on the corner.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A sand filled Falsterbo
entries.summary: Around 1900 neither the squares or streets were set in stone.
entries.description: Around 1900 neither the squares or streets were set in stone. It was just regular sand, not even hardened. Deep tracks were created by the wagons that struggled to pull themselves through the streets. It was said the Falsterboians had a shuffling way of walking as they dragged their wooden slippers through the sand! In the next picture the square has changed, but it is still not set in stone. That most likely happened at the same time as the little fountain with the statue Gåsatös was installed in the summer of 1956.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Peace in Skanör
entries.summary: Here on Dykerigatan you'll find a part of Skanör that was not affected by the fires.
entries.description: Here on Dykerigatan you'll find a part of Skanör that was not affected by the fires. All houses are still standing. This area called Möen made it from both the catastrophes in 1874 and 1885 together with Rådhustorget.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Mill with geese
entries.summary: Postcards were made of this picture for 60 years!
entries.description: Postcards were made of this picture for 60 years! One reason is probably the geese, but another is because the picture could never be taken again. The next picture shows the reason. The last miller canceled the lease in 1922. Thereafter the mill decayed so much it no longer looked good in pictures. As it decayed it could still be found in all its glory in postcards.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Midsummer of 1902
entries.summary: An old picture from the Midsummer of 1902.
entries.description: An old picture from the Midsummer of 1902. There was a meadow on the north side of Mellangatan where all of Skanör gathered to decorate the maypole. Many Skanör celebrities can be seen in the picture. At least three of the brothers åberg and of course the famous carpenter Landgren and about 90 other Skanörians
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Falsterbo square with a cow
entries.summary: The Old Square with sand and wood.
entries.description: The Old Square with sand and wood. A lone cow is sauntering about down towards Södergatan, and a little girl is standing alone and a little abandoned in the square. Perhaps it is the photographer's daughter that gets to act as motive.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Cows in the streets
entries.summary: Cows in the streets The picture shows Mellangatan seen from Hamngatan.
entries.description: Cows in the streets The picture shows Mellangatan seen from Hamngatan. However, Hamngatan does not continue down to the right towards the docks. To fix this, the little house to the right was torn down and they had to straighten out the road network. This explains why Claes Albert Landgren's house on the current corner to the right is the only one with straight corners, while the others are cut. The house simply wasn't a corner house when it was built.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skanör's mill
entries.summary: The mill could have originated in the 16th century, but it has been rebuilt and renovated many times since.
entries.description: The mill could have originated in the 16th century, but it has been rebuilt and renovated many times since. A beam has been dated back to around 1700. In any case it is one of Skåne's oldest mills. It is a stump mill. Basically, it is standing on a bearing "stump" so that all of the mill house "bellow" is facing the wind. These mills were succeeded during the 1800s by the so-called Dutchmen, where only the "bonnet" with the wings is turned towards the wind.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skanör's station
entries.summary: The second to last stop on the Vellinge-Skanör-Falsterbo track.
entries.description: The second to last stop on the Vellinge-Skanör-Falsterbo track. All station houses were designed by the cathedral-architect Theodor Wåhlin, who also designed the main building of Falsterbo House. The image shows opening day on May 18th, 1914. Large parts of the town s population have lined up to be photographed. The next picture shows the station with a kiosk from the 1940s and the last picture shows a farewell to Skanör in the 1920s.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Villa Tallarna
entries.summary: Villa Tallarna at Fyrvägen.
entries.description: Villa Tallarna at Fyrvägen. The house was built at the beginning of the century in a bourgeois style. It was renovated sometime during the 1930s, but this time as a functionalist villa. The side entrance on the garden side still hints the old style from the turn of the 20th century.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Sjögatan/Sjövägen
entries.summary: A town was a marketplace and needed a border around itself.
entries.description: A town was a marketplace and needed a border around itself. This had been the way since the early Middle Ages. Even in 1905 there were still gates left in Falsterbo (they did after all keep cows and sheep away from the streets!). The gate emphasized town and land by having the street change name from Sjögatan to Sjövägen. We look upon the square. All the houses are still there in renovated conditions.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Strandbadsvägen
entries.summary: Strandbadsvägen from a not yet grown Falsterbo.
entries.description: Strandbadsvägen from a not yet grown Falsterbo. The girl seems to be standing in what is now The Pear Alley. It is the photographer's daughter standing there in a somewhat strange outfit. She is visible on all of his postcards from Skanör and Falsterbo, although in Skanör she is dressed in a folk dress!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A UFO has landed
entries.summary: Hotel Falsterbo House entrance.
entries.description: Hotel Falsterbo House entrance. When the building was finished, it could be seen all throughout Falsterbonäset. It was 4 stories high during a time when few buildings in Falsterbo had more than one. The first picture is most likely taken during the opening year of 1908. In the next picture a railroad from the station on the other side of Fyrvägen has been added. The third picture is from after 1913 when the Annex was built. A casino was built to the left of the main building simultaneously. Although that is not visible in this picture.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Hotel Falsterbo House
entries.summary: Hotel Falsterbo House was built by the railroad company in 1908.
entries.description: Hotel Falsterbo House was built by the railroad company in 1908. When it needed to expand in 1912 it became its own company Falsterbo Havsbad AB. The Restaurant Man Moje Björkman took over the company after a few years and made the House into something truly special. Nice rooms, good food, beach and swimming, tennis, riding, golf, concerts, the-dancing in the afternoons, balls, and more. It was all dancing on the ceiling and the high life. There have been several other owners since then. Many surely remember Lars Lendrops time in the 1960s. Today it is all residential areas, and silence has fallen over Falsterbo House.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Falsterbo’s schools
entries.summary: Falsterbo old school, that is also to say new school, on picture number two from 1912 is now old and has become a parish house.
entries.description: Falsterbo old school, that is also to say new school, on picture number two from 1912 is now old and has become a parish house. The white school building was designed by Johan Angelin in 1912 in the same style as Hotel Falsterbo House and the stations. The inspiration came from the old churches in the old Danish Skåne. The last time this style was used should have been the Baltic exhibition in Malmö in 1914. Designed by Ferdinand Boberg. Then World War I arrived, and the world was never the same.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Hjalmar Gullberg
entries.summary: The estate closest to your right is Villa Lundhem, which Hjalmar Gullberg inherited in 1928.
entries.description: The estate closest to your right is Villa Lundhem, which Hjalmar Gullberg inherited in 1928. He was a writer and poet and a member of the Swedish Academy 1940-1961. Gullberg spent many summers here writing poems with motifs from Falsterbonäset. Here Anders österling, Olle Holmberg, Frans G Bengtsson, Ivar Harrie, and many others met and spent time together with family.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Boarding House Kiellgren
entries.summary: There were a lot of boarding houses in Falsterbo mainly during the 1920s, 30s, and 40s.
entries.description: There were a lot of boarding houses in Falsterbo mainly during the 1920s, 30s, and 40s. Olympia, Godegård, Villa Margaretha, and more. Here, on the corner of Fädriften and Gåsgatan, Kiellgren s boarding house was situated during the 1910s and 20s. The text Cow street [ Kogatan ] on one of the cards is just a paraphrase of Fädriften.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Fiddeledet
entries.summary: Two villas by the golf course and Fiddeledet.
entries.description: Two villas by the golf course and Fiddeledet. The villa to the left has received a medieval flare with timbered framing and small windows. The right one should have a nice view of the golf course and the sea from all the windows.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Norregård in Gröna torg
entries.summary: Storgatan by Gröna torg.
entries.description: Storgatan by Gröna torg. To your right is Norregård from the 18th century that became the postmen s holiday house and thereafter hotel and conference facility. A few years back it became a residential area.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The first villas
entries.summary: Villas by the ruin. Malmros (1909), Bentz (1904), and Pfannenstills (1907) villas.
entries.description: Villas by the ruin. Malmros (1909), Bentz (1904), and Pfannenstills (1907) villas. The first two remain standing. In the Pfannenstillian villa, amongst others, princess Sybilla often lived with the little princesses Margareta, Birgitta, D sir e, Christina, and with time our current king, Carl Gustav.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Torn down palaces
entries.summary: Here we can see two houses built around 1910.
entries.description: Here we can see two houses built around 1910. Both were torn down in the 1950s. They were built on damp ground and moldered away. The closest villa is Villa Margarete. The Falsterbo photographer Matilda Månsson was hired to take a few pictures that the owners turned into postcards. The house in the back switched between being called the Axelsonian Villa and Villa Solhaga.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Villa Queckfeldt
entries.summary: Villa Queckfeldt. Designed by the cathedral-architect Theodor Wåhlin for engineer Queckfeldt in 1910
entries.description: Villa Queckfeldt. Designed by the cathedral-architect Theodor Wåhlin for engineer Queckfeldt in 1910
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A pink pastry
entries.summary: Villa Tångvallen. A magnificent pink pastry in art nouveau style.
entries.description: Villa Tångvallen. A magnificent pink pastry in art nouveau style. The architect Alfred Grenander designed the house for himself and his family in 1907. The whole building has now been renovated and every detail has gotten freshened up. Grenander also designed Wertheim on Storgatan in Falsterbo and Villa Solglimt in Skanör. Otherwise he is most famous in Berlin where he designed a number of subways in the typical art nouveau style.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A villa yellow as the sun
entries.summary: Villa Solglimt. Designed by Alfred Grenander and built in 1910.
entries.description: Villa Solglimt. Designed by Alfred Grenander and built in 1910. Grenander has also designed Wertheim on Storgatan and Villa Tångvallen in Falsterbo. Otherwise he is most famous in Berlin where he designed a number of subways in the typical art nouveau style.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The Assembly House
entries.summary: The building has old ancestry.
entries.description: The building has old ancestry. It was built sometime before 1876 by initiative of the then current assembly in Falsterbo. A hundred years later they were merged with the assembly in Malmö and in 1979 the preaching was over.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The smallest liquor store in Sweden
entries.summary: Liquor once upon a time was bought at Gästis, but then the drinks got their own store here on östergatan.
entries.description: Liquor once upon a time was bought at Gästis, but then the drinks got their own store here on östergatan. Still in the 1960s it was the smallest liquor store in Sweden. After a move to the square by ICA with the construction market as the closest neighbor, business finally started sprawling. The population grew, but it grew even more in Höllviken which eventually won the tug of war over the municipality s two only liquor stores. The other one is in Vellinge. The picture of the interior is from around 1910 and is taken when the store was situated on Hammargatan by the City Hall - Rådhustorget.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Falsterbo House jetty
entries.summary: The jetty unfortunately no longer exists.
entries.description: The jetty unfortunately no longer exists. Nowadays there is another one a bit further east. Here are a few pictures from back when the jetty was full of the House s guests, and only guests the public was not allowed.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skanör’s Gästis
entries.summary: There has stood an inn in Skanör since the beginning of the 1800s.
entries.description: There has stood an inn in Skanör since the beginning of the 1800s. The current building is from 1887. Known restaurant owners, cooks, and guests have passed through for the approximately 250 years it has existed. However, up until the 1900s only food and a simple bed was given to the customers, and of course a change of horses. The stagecoach started going from Vellinge in 1886. That s when tourism came to life and the demand for food and room increased.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Panorama from the station
entries.summary: A panorama from 1910 consisting of four postcards photographed by the Falsterbo photographer Matilda Månson.
entries.description: A panorama from 1910 consisting of four postcards photographed by the Falsterbo photographer Matilda Månson.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Pär i Vången
entries.summary: Pär i Vången stands alone in Skanör s town park.
entries.description: Pär i Vången stands alone in Skanör s town park. The front towards Vånggatan is the oldest. The plot has several edges, with a little stream running through it although it only has water in it in the spring and autumn.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Söderlindhska estate
entries.summary: The estate was a beautiful quadrilateral Skåne estate, like many others in Skanör.
entries.description: The estate was a beautiful quadrilateral Skåne estate, like many others in Skanör. But after the fires of 1874 and 1885 only a few were left. Unfortunately, more fire was to come. The Söderlindhska estate burned down in 1921 and the plot was thereafter deserted for more than 50 years.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The girls that disappeared
entries.summary: Never trust old pictures!
entries.description: Never trust old pictures! The photographers always edited their pictures. We can see an example here. First, a picture of three girls dressed fashionably around the 1910s. The next picture shows the girls against an algae moat with the mill in the background. The last picture shows the algae moat and the mill, but without the girls. The reason is the mill. It stood and decayed. That s why the photographer took an old picture and edited out the girls. They were no longer dressed according to the times as the picture was used again in the 1930s. But if you look closely the shadow of the standing girl is left on the ground!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Turisthotellet?
entries.summary: It is only Skanör s inn that for a time around the 1910s hid behind the name Turisthotellet.
entries.description: It is only Skanör s inn that for a time around the 1910s hid behind the name Turisthotellet. To the left you can see Gamlegård. Despite the estate standing right in the crossfire of the flames during both of the large fires in the 1800s, it made it without a scratch.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Crowds at the station
entries.summary: There was a railroad to Skanör and Falsterbo from Malmö through Vellinge between the years of 1904 and 1971.
entries.description: There was a railroad to Skanör and Falsterbo from Malmö through Vellinge between the years of 1904 and 1971. This is a picture from 1911. The heyday of the railroad was the 1930s and 40s. Every Sunday a steam-engine went from Malmö down towards Falsterbo with beach guests. The Bath Train was only half the price of the normal one. With time, it became the last regular steam-engine left in Sweden, and it remained until 1965.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The Casino
entries.summary: Falsterbo House Casino was to the left of the entrance.
entries.description: Falsterbo House Casino was to the left of the entrance. It was built in 1912 and torn down in 1968. It was no gambling hall; here revues were held and you ate, listened to concerts, and danced. Outside, a pool was built in 1934. Sweden s first one at a hotel.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Military Prayer in Skanör
entries.summary: A strange picture taken by the Falsterbo photographer Matilda Månson.
entries.description: A strange picture taken by the Falsterbo photographer Matilda Månson. We see soldiers and a man playing the organ. This is most likely during the military readiness in 1914. World War I has broken out and Sweden is mobilizing. On Sunday the military hosts a Military Prayer, in other words a mass. All of it is taking place on the large meadow north of Skanör s station with the locals as an audience.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: At port
entries.summary: Skanör s port came to be in 1881, but has been dredged several times.
entries.description: Skanör s port came to be in 1881, but has been dredged several times. The sand mainly moves with the big autumn storms and changes the depth and location of the sand dunes. The port has changed from work to leisure time. The old fishing boats made of wood are gone and sailboats and motorboats in plastic have taken over. The port has also become a tourist attraction with several restaurants, kiosks, and ice cream bars.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The cement factory in Skanör's harbor
entries.summary: How does one have the idea to build a cement factory in Skanör s harbor?
entries.description: How does one have the idea to build a cement factory in Skanör s harbor? There is no lime and no mud here, the main ingredients in cement. Everything has to be imported from the Danish Möön. However, it was built and finished in the late summer of 1914, right before World War I began. It didn t become a success. When the business was decommissioned in 1919, a share of 500 Swedish crowns gave one Swedish crown back!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Blå Bandet [The Blue Ribbon]
entries.summary: Skanörs Blå Band-association was built in 1911.
entries.description: Skanörs Blå Band-association was built in 1911. It is an association that was brought to Sweden in 1883 and stands for complete sobriety. This has also been a cinema and a police office.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Bain de Mer de Falsterbo
entries.summary: An advertisement short with French subtitles for Falsterbo House in the 1920s.
entries.description: An advertisement short with French subtitles for Falsterbo House in the 1920s. The owner of the house was the Restaurant Man Moje Björkman, and his wife Magda Björkman to the right and her sister Andy Andir are the ones sitting in the beach basket. Beneath them lies Magda and Moje's daughters Lilly and Ninny. Observe the nanny that has been forced to hide in the bath house. Working from the shadows .
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The bathing huts
entries.summary: The colorful bath huts can be seen a long way and give a nice break for the eye between beach and sea.
entries.description: The colorful bath huts can be seen a long way and give a nice break for the eye between beach and sea. However, it s the same picture every year with the October storms that nags the beach and makes the small huts fall over. Picture number 2 shows how it could have looked in the 1920s at the north sand dune.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Hans Petters gården
entries.summary: The picture was taken here between Hotel Gässlingen and the church wall in the 1930s.
entries.description: The picture was taken here between Hotel Gässlingen and the church wall in the 1930s. Hans Pettersgården was one of the oldest estates in Skanör. Unfortunately it was torn down in 1961.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Kolabacken
entries.summary: Kolabacken is an old lighthouse area where they burned coal in a basket on a tipping rod.
entries.description: Kolabacken is an old lighthouse area where they burned coal in a basket on a tipping rod. In time it became quite the slope (if you ask the people of Skåne.) It is debated for how long the lighthouse stood here. The memorial stone says 1222, but others say this is wrong and claim that the early 17th century is more probable.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The popular Strandbaden
entries.summary: Strandbaden (a specific bathing place) opened in 1928.
entries.description: Strandbaden (a specific bathing place) opened in 1928. This is the old building that burned to the ground in 2006. The current building is from 2008. It was the railway company that originally created Strandbaden so that regular workers and officials could come down to bathe, eat, danse, and of course take the train both there and back again.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Josef Frank’s terms
entries.summary: Villa Cla son is one of the six houses that the famous architect and designer Josef Frank designed in Sweden.
entries.description: Villa Cla son is one of the six houses that the famous architect and designer Josef Frank designed in Sweden. All of them are here in Falsterbo: Villa Cla son 1927, Bernt L dkes väg 10; Villa Carlsten 1927, Fyrvägen 26; Villa Seth 1934, Fyrvägen 13; Anders österling Writing Den 1934, Fiddeledet; Villa Låftman 1934, Fyrvägen 15; Villa Wehtje 1936, Kung Olofs väg 1. When it came to design, Josef Frank cooperated with Estrid Ericson, founder of Svensk Tenn. Mostly they created furniture and a lot of patterns and fabrics.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The slides
entries.summary: The railroad between Vellinge and Skanör Falsterbo did not run with a profit.
entries.description: The railroad between Vellinge and Skanör Falsterbo did not run with a profit. What to do? A bathing spot was built for the working people. Unlike the nice Falsterbo House where you were not allowed to change directly on the beach, but needed a bath house. Strandbaden opened during the summer of 1928 with both a dancefloor, restaurant, and slide. It cost 10 Swedish cents to ride the big one. You see, a mat was needed to sit on, or your behind would burn. Although young boys soon realized that when the orderly wasn t around one might as well go down the slide on a piece of algae! The slides disappeared during the icy winters of the war that ruined the bases.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Josef in the wall
entries.summary: The first picture shows the house completely newly built in 1914.
entries.description: The first picture shows the house completely newly built in 1914. In the second picture, a stair leading up to the entrance has been added. The cellar has simultaneously been turned into a store that, according to the sign, sells southern goods, groceries, and chocolate. The store manager's name was Josef Andersson, but he was called Josef in the wall. The building also became a hostel. In time it even became a hotel under the name Spelabäcken. Today it is an office hotel.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Geese in Hammargatan
entries.summary: The junction between Hammargatan and Mellangatan.
entries.description: The junction between Hammargatan and Mellangatan. Back in the day the geese walked around freely in the streets of Skanör and Falsterbo. Today it is a bit more organized. Do not walk too close by when they have their younglings with them. They can be quite hostile towards people!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The typographer's sanatorium
entries.summary: When living at Malmö typographer's sanatorium, strict rules were to be followed.
entries.description: When living at Malmö typographer's sanatorium, strict rules were to be followed. For example: 4. Books, magazines, and journals, which are to be handled with care, are not to be brought outside the locales of the Home, and shall at once after use be correctly folded and placed in its predetermined place. 10. It should be the point of honor of all guests not to depreciate the esteem of the Typograph Corps and the Home. The text was written when the house opened in 1952, and was probably old fashioned even then. It's as if it has been plucked out of Grönköpings weekly paper.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Solidarity in Skanör
entries.summary: It is a private house today, but for a long time Solidar was the largest grocery store in Skanör.
entries.description: It is a private house today, but for a long time Solidar was the largest grocery store in Skanör. Even during the early 1900s a store named Coop existed. However, Solidar never managed to become Konsum before it was shut down. The competition from ICA became too big.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The triangle that became a roundabout
entries.summary: The flat concrete road from Ljunghusen turns left towards Falsterbo and right towards Skanör.
entries.description: The flat concrete road from Ljunghusen turns left towards Falsterbo and right towards Skanör. No large amount of traffic in the 1940s. A candy shop and a phone booth. There is a vegetable salesman to the left. Today the triangle has become a roundabout.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A rural square
entries.summary: This is Gamla torg in all its rural glory in the 1940s.
entries.description: This is Gamla torg in all its rural glory in the 1940s. To the left you can see down Södergatan towards the station. Behind the kiosk lies Conditoriträdgården.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Villa by Kolabacken
entries.summary: Villa Pilevall, neighbour with Kolabacken, with a view of Falsterbo golf course.
entries.description: Villa Pilevall, neighbour with Kolabacken, with a view of Falsterbo golf course.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Lillstugans Café
entries.summary: Here, Caf Lillstugan was situated during the 1940s and 50s.
entries.description: Here, Caf Lillstugan was situated during the 1940s and 50s. It wasn t big, but it was nice.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A museum rich in content
entries.summary: Falsterbo museum came to be in 1930.
entries.description: Falsterbo museum came to be in 1930. The current museum building is from 1940. This is where Skanör and Falsterbo s histories from the Middle Ages to the present are told. The lifeboat 416 stood in the museum for 45 years, but has now been renovated and moved to Skanör's docks.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skanör begins here
entries.summary: The houses are the same, but a mall has been added to the right, which has moved the city center from Mellangatan to Bäckatorget to the right.
entries.description: The houses are the same, but a mall has been added to the right, which has moved the city center from Mellangatan to Bäckatorget to the right. Everything is now gathered in one place; healthcare, pharmacy, library, bank, construction marker, supermarket, etc.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Studentgården
entries.summary: Doctor John af Klerker and his wife, professor Edla af Klerker, lived on the corner of Västergatan and Kyrkogatan in Skanör.
entries.description: Doctor John af Klerker and his wife, professor Edla af Klerker, lived on the corner of Västergatan and Kyrkogatan in Skanör. After John and Edla passed away the estate was bequeathed to Akademiska Föreningen in Lund in 1938. When the students took over the estate the faithful servant of 24 years, Miss Emma Jönsson, came included as housekeeper. Her salary was paid through an amendment to the will.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Dykerigatan
entries.summary: Here on Dykerigatan you'll find a part of Skanör that was not affected by the fires.
entries.description: Here on Dykerigatan you'll find a part of Skanör that was not affected by the fires. All houses are still standing. This area called Möen made it from both the catastrophes in 1874 and 1885 together with Rådhustorget.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Movie set
entries.summary: Edvard Persson plays a cop in the movie Skanör and Falsterbo, 1983.
entries.description: Edvard Persson plays a cop in the movie Skanör and Falsterbo, 1983. Behind him stands the old liquor store on östergatan. It is also a general picture from the shoot and the cinema poster for the movie in 1939.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Lumberyard became a construction market
entries.summary: Back in the day, by what is now called Axelsons torg, lay a lumberyard that through the years had changing names: Ta i Trä (Knock on Wood), Kock s construction market.
entries.description: Back in the day, by what is now called Axelsons torg, lay a lumberyard that through the years had changing names: Ta i Trä (Knock on Wood), Kock s construction market. In time it became an assortment of iron goods, sunbeds, and other things that both summer guests and permanent residents found useful.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: A fisherman’s cottage with a rich history
entries.summary: The fisherman Karl Larsson and his wife bought the house in 1881.
entries.description: The fisherman Karl Larsson and his wife bought the house in 1881. But since his wife died after a difficult childbirth in 1897 he was left alone with six children who all grew up here in the cottage. Except for a residence, this place has also been a preschool for poor children and a library. The library moved into the more spacious station house after the railroad s closure in 1971. Nowadays there is a gallery in the cottage. On the other two pictures, östergatan runs on the wrong side of the building. From here to the station back then there was no street, only a large meadow with a footpath.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Market day at Fädriften
entries.summary: Despite all the squares in Falsterbo, not a lot of square trade has been going on during the centuries.
entries.description: Despite all the squares in Falsterbo, not a lot of square trade has been going on during the centuries. But on a meadow close to the station there was life and movement after the war and up until the 1970s.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Hotel Falsterbo House entrance
entries.summary: A picture facing Falsterbo House's hotel entrance.
entries.description: A picture facing Falsterbo House's hotel entrance. The hotel and restaurant were closed long ago. The whole complex is now a residential area.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The boss's villa became a disco
entries.summary: Falsterbogården was originally home of the boss of the railroad company, but later came to be a boarding house with different names.
entries.description: Falsterbogården was originally home of the boss of the railroad company, but later came to be a boarding house with different names. In the 1960s and 70s it was a disco going, amongst others, by the name Butterfly. Soon thereafter it was torn down and instead residential areas were built on the premises.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Just regular water
entries.summary: Clean water has always been important.
entries.description: Clean water has always been important. Before bacteria and germs were understood, water was life threatening to drink. You drank beer instead. The wells were often missing their "shell". Because of this all sorts of waste flowed into the wells when it was raining. This shell is for the cattle. For example, cows on their way back to the farm after grazing. There was also a watering hole for the animals in all villages. Often in the middle of the village. There are none left anymore in Skanör and Falsterbo. It was necessary especially for geese and ducks. You see, they can only mate in water!
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The salvage company
entries.summary: Dykerigatan got its name from Dykerigården.
entries.description: Dykerigatan got its name from Dykerigården. Dykerikompaniet's task was to take care of wrecks, beached ships and its goods. Goods and timber were auctioned out and the company received their cut. The original building burned down in 1874. The current building is of a younger date. The second picture shows the estate to the left around 1910. To the right Gamlegård, which survived both the large fires, can be seen.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Conditoriträdgården
entries.summary: Södergatan leading to Gamla torg.
entries.description: Södergatan leading to Gamla torg. To the left lay Conditoriträdgården. When the owner became too old to take care of it, the building stood and decayed for a long time. Cookie jars etc always remained and reminded people of a time when summer guests munched on Danish Pastry and drank coffee or refreshing lemonade. The original estate was built in 1876 and torn down in the 1980s.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Bror Bengtsson’s groceries
entries.summary: Bror Bengtsson was one of the last of the old tribe of grocery sellers.
entries.description: Bror Bengtsson was one of the last of the old tribe of grocery sellers. In picture number two he is standing behind the counter in the store on östergatan. The ad read: grocery- and miscellaneous store. Porcelain and Kitchen goods as well as dairy products. Phone. 202. Today the whole counter can be seen with goods from the Falsterbo museum.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Rådhuset
entries.summary: Så här såg Landskronas första rådhus ut.
entries.description: Så här såg Landskronas första rådhus ut. Det medeltida huset revs 1881, ett par år innan det nuvarande rådhuset byggdes. Bilden är tagen år 1880 av en okänd fotograf och är från Landskrona museums samling.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The old railway station
entries.summary: At the end of August 1885, Selma Lagerlöf steps off the train in Landskrona to begin her first position as a teacher at Landskrona's elementary school for girls.
entries.description: At the end of August 1885, Selma Lagerlöf steps off the train in Landskrona to begin her first position as a teacher at Landskrona's elementary school for girls.

entries.description: Selma Lagerlöf's first residence in Landskrona was with the then-owner of the house, customs officer Carl Gustaf Wilhelm von D ben, from 1885 to 1886.

entries.name: Storgatan 13
entries.summary: Here in the corner of Storgatan and Stora Strandgatan was located a "Wine & Delicacy Shop." The house was owned by And.
entries.description: Here in the corner of Storgatan and Stora Strandgatan was located a "Wine & Delicacy Shop." The house was owned by And. S. Cronberg from 1893. The next building, which was also part of Falken 5, housed a shoemaker's workshop. Following that was the house where Selma Lagerlöf lived as a lodger with the widow Frederikke Rönne from 1886 to 1889.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.summary: "Gamla Bryggan," which housed Landskrona's elementary school for girls from 1871 to 1915.
entries.description: "Gamla Bryggan," which housed Landskrona's elementary school for girls from 1871 to 1915. Selma lived in the school's attic apartment from 1888 to 1893.

entries.description: Från början kallades huset för Björkegrens villa eftersom det var stadsfiskalen Anders Björkegrens hem. Senare blev Böttchers caf . Bilden är från Landskrona museums samling.

entries.description: Kanalen mellem Dok en og Frederiksholm set fra Frederiksholm ca. 1895. I forgrunden chefen for Orlogsv rftets dampbarkasse med kontreadmiralen Carl Bruun i f rd med stige i land på Frederiksholm. I midten S artilleriets kontorbygning. Tv. Dokkens maskinhus.

entries.description: Mellan 1827 och 1940 användes Citadellet som fängelse. Fängelsebyggnaden som du ser på bilden tillkom först på 1860-talet och revs 1964. Bilden du ser är tagen år 1900 och är från Landskrona museums samling.

entries.description: Bilden visar Teaterparken innan Landskrona teaters tillkomst 1901. Teaterparken hade även ett annat namn från början, den kallades för Neesska trädgård eller Neessaparken eftersom grosshandlaren C.J. Neess ägde parken en gång i tiden. Bilden är från Landskrona museums samling.

entries.name: Strandpaviljongen
entries.summary: 1892 byggdes Strandpaviljongen, ett initiativ av Carl Tranchell, kallad sockerkungen.
entries.description: 1892 byggdes Strandpaviljongen, ett initiativ av Carl Tranchell, kallad sockerkungen. Det var ett led i Landskronas utveckling till badort, och tanken var att erbjuda förfriskningar till badare. Det passade med placeringen vid den långa bryggan med Nya kallbadhuset och promenadstråket Linjen längs kusten. Varmbadhuset låg också nära.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.description: Så här såg Norra Långgatan ut omkring början av 1900-talet. Korsvirkeshuset till vänster ersattes 1914 med ett nybyggt Post- och telegrafhus. Fotot ur Landskrona museums samling.

Husen är i funktionalistisk stil med enkla geometriska grundformer, avskalade släta ljusa fasader och platta tak. I mars 1933 hölls utställningen Det moderna hemmet i sju radhus på ålstensgatan. entries.name: Vatten och Krattor
entries.summary: - Hjälp till här! En gestalt i grå arbetskläder står framför Milo.
entries.description: - Hjälp till här! En gestalt i grå arbetskläder står framför Milo. En till död människa som vill prata ? - Hörru, hugg i här! - Menar du mig? undrar Milo. - Ja, vem annars? Jag måste ställa av de här vattenhinkarna och det är tungt serru. Här är många törstiga blommor. - Vattenhinkar? - Ja, det är ett evigt släpande från vattenbrunnen. Jag brukar ha bra med hjälp, men nu är vi kort om folk. Blommor ska planteras, rabatter vattnas, och där borta ska en grav grävas. Det är bara att ta en spade och börja. Imorgon ska det vara klart. Det måste vara Trädgårdsmästaren. - Har du somnat? Det är bara att börja! - Nej tack Jag tror inte det. - Tack och Nej? Hörru, du kan sluta skämta och börja gräva. Här har du en spade. Graven ska vara rymlig, hela kistan ska få plats. Ingen urna från krematoriet den här gången. - Krematoriet ? - Ja, krematoriet där borta. Milo lämnar snabbt trädgårdsarbete och grävande, och skyndar mot krematoriet.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Sorgeträdet
entries.summary: Ett träd med hängande grenar väntar på Milo.
entries.description: Ett träd med hängande grenar väntar på Milo. Ja, väntar. - är jag verkligen sorglig? är jag inte bara vacker? Och lugn? Många namn har jag. Tårpil är jag ofta. I urgamla berättelser sägs min kåda vara tårar som förvandlas till bärnsten. Men, du kan kalla mig Sorgeträdet. Här är lugnt. Milo sätter sig intill trädets stam och andas ut. - Om du var ett träd, vilket träd skulle du vara då? frågar Sorgeträdet. - Eh ett äpplen! Milo tänker på äpplena i en trädgård: - Ett äppelträd. - Jaha, ett rikt träd. Både vackra blommor och god frukt. Smart! Och, vem skulle du vilja minnas? Det känns lätt att prata med Sorgeträdet. - Du förstår, fortsätter Trädet, så FORT vi tänker på de döda så finns de. Så TäNK nu! Milo tänker. Saker som de gjort tillsammans dyker upp, en speciell doft finns där, skämten, och skratten och deras favoriträtt. - Du minns. De finns. Leta en plats där du kan minnas. Skriv ned namnet på den du vill minnas och häng det i ett träd. Ditt träd. Milo reser sig och spanar mot ett eget träd längre bort.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Att minnas
entries.summary: Instruktion till dig som deltar: Leta upp en plats där du kan sitta ned och minnas.
entries.description: Instruktion till dig som deltar: Leta upp en plats där du kan sitta ned och minnas. Tänk på den du vill minnas. Vem är det? Dyker det upp någon doft i ditt minne? En färg kanske? Eller en röst? Minns du någonting som ni gjort tillsammans? Någonting som har hänt? Skriv ned namnet på den du vill minnas. Skriv ned ditt minne. Du kan skriva det för dig själv. Och du kan dela det med någon. Så fort vi tänker på dem så finns de.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Milo möter begravningsplatsen
entries.summary: - Vi ska bara hämta blommorna.
entries.description: - Vi ska bara hämta blommorna. Gå före du Milo, så ses vi vid minneslunden. Det är alltid så tråkigt när familjen ska åka hit, det händer ingenting, tänker Milo. Och det känns så bestämt hur allt ska vara här. Och hur man ska bete sig, och inte bete sig. Alltså, det är ingen som säger detta, det liksom bara finns där, som en tyst outtalad regel Milo spanar ut över begravningsplatsen. Så stor den är där den sträcker ut sig som en enorm trädgård. Milo får syn på en bänk långt, långt borta. Där kan jag äntligen vara för mig själv, tänker Milo och ger sig av.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Träd i rad
entries.summary: - Vi har sett många människor komma längs den här vägen.
entries.description: - Vi har sett många människor komma längs den här vägen. Milo stannar upp, vilka är det nu som talar? - Vi har hört många människoröster; lågmälda, högljudda, barn och vuxna. Milo följer trädens stammar med blicken och sedan uppåt, uppåt mot trädkronorna. - Vi är Träd i rad, vi är all er, vi står som pelargångar och visar vägen till kapellet där begravningsceremonin sker. Ett mummel ljuder omkring Milo. Eller, är det träden som susar? Milo letar sig framåt, framåt mellan träden... Det vindlar, verkar aldrig ta slut, träd efter träd efter träd - Vi är fortsättningen. Vi kan bli äldre än ni. Ofta finns vi innan ni föds. Vi ger er en känsla av trygghet, bara genom att vara Träd. - HITTAR DU TILL KAPELLET NU? Ett stort träd [med mörk röst] lutar sig över Milo och verkar vilja hjälpa till - Tack, jag går själv! svarar Milo snabbt och ger sig av för att hitta kapellet.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Skogskapellet
entries.summary: Ok, det här måste vara kapellet.
entries.description: Ok, det här måste vara kapellet. - Här sker ceremonin innan kroppen, eller askan, begravs. Milo känner den där vinden igen. Det är främlingen. - Här kan vi hedra och minnas den som inte lever längre. Främlingen är tillbaka. Det känns som ett vänligt sällskap: - Ser du alla stenarna, gravstenarna? Som en liten skog av stenar, tänker Milo och blir avbruten: - Finn! Finn mig! Här! Här är jag! En försiktig röst hörs från ett helt annat håll. - Okey! Jag ska leta. Milo hör sig själv prata högt och känner hur benen rör sig åt det håll som Rösten kommer ifrån.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: Graven
entries.summary: - Vem är jag? undrar Rösten, Vem är jag som ligger här?
entries.description: - Vem är jag? undrar Rösten, Vem är jag som ligger här? Vilken grav! Milo står framför en stor grav och på gravstenen finns en enkel namnteckning. - Ja, de har gjort en fin plats till mig. Så stor. Jag var rätt blyg, inte så glad för uppmärksamhet. Men jag tyckte om film, och fiktion. Framför kameran var jag djärv. Jag föddes i Sverige och dog i New York. En Movie Star. Det var jag. Känd över hela världen helt enkelt. Om jag själv fick välja skulle jag ha en liten enkel grav i skymundan, nära skogen och trädgårdsmästaren. Men allt bestämmer vi inte, säger Rösten, med en liten suck. - Vänta! Men Rösten har redan försvunnit. Och ändå, det känns som om Milo har lärt känna någon litegrand. - Vem är du? Ingen svarar. - Hallå?!!! Det är tyst. Så kommer en sista försiktig viskning: - Kommer du att minnas mig? Skriv mitt namn: Greta Garbo. Och hitta Trädgårdsmästaren! Trädgårdsmästaren. Vatten kratta blomvaser Milo letar sig mot servicestationen.
key_facts: Historisk plats ur Be Here Then

entries.name: The Train Station
entries.summary: Today, being able to travel across the Skåne region in an hour or so is a given - but before the railway was finished your only option was pretty much to go by
entries.description: Today, being able to travel across the Skåne region in an hour or so is a given - but before the railway was finished your only option was pretty much to go by horse-drawn carriage, which could take several days. So you can imagine that when the railway to Hässleholm was finished in 1860 and going down to Malmö suddenly only took around three hours, it was seen as something truly revolutionising. The importance of the railway for Hässleholm as a city can hardly be overstated: Thanks to the railway people started moving here in increasing numbers. Hässleholm became an important travel hub, with many hotels despite its modest size, and a bustling city centre market. That the railway station ended up being built here rather than somewhere else along the tracks wasn't pure coincidence however - the aristocratic Ehrenborg family donated some of the land belonging Hässleholmsgården , a manor in their possession. The railway station has been remodeled and expanded several times. The first picture is a very old photography, from the 1860's, taken soon after it was built. The second picture depicts the station after its expansion during the 1920's, and as you can see in the third picture things have changed inside as well. The fourth picture shows a famous actor called Edvard Persson, visiting Hässleholm. He was famous during the 1930's and 1940's, and was often cast as a infallibly jovial and down to earth - qualities that in a Swedish context are still in many ways associated with people in Skåne, perhaps thanks to Edvard Persson.

entries.name: Trobecks pensionat
entries.summary: Vittsjö är ju känt som gammal kurort och hade i det avseendet sina glansdagar under första halvan av 1900-talet, då det som mest fanns omkring fyrtio pensionat här.
entries.description: Vittsjö är ju känt som gammal kurort och hade i det avseendet sina glansdagar under första halvan av 1900-talet, då det som mest fanns omkring fyrtio pensionat här. Ungefär tio år efter att tågförbindelsen kommit till Vittsjö (1890) blev det trendigt att åka och kurera sig i bland annat Göingetrakten, och folk började vallfärda till pensionaten. Något som särskilt verkar ha lockat stadsbor till besök var meddelandet om att den "ozonrika luften" som fanns här skulle vara särskilt välgörande för hälsan. För lockade blev de verkligen: I början av 1900-talet kom de i såna mängder att det tiotal pensionat som fanns i Vittsjö alltid var helt fullbokade under sommaren, ibland ett år eller mer i förväg. För att åtminstone delvis lösa detta lyxproblem ordnade de som bodde i villor nära pensionaten med husrum åt besökare som annars inte fått plats. Christine Bern från Malmö var den första som registrerades som ägare till pensionat på orten, och om namnet låter bekant så är det förmodligen för att hon var släkt med ägarna till Berns hotell som fortfarande finns i Stockholm, men som också fanns i Hässleholm fram till mitten på 1900-talet. Namnet "Trobecks" fick det hör pensionatet efter Artur Trobeck som köpte fastigheten 1936. Att bilden är tagen under början av 1900-talet kan vi se tack vare en liten, men viktig, detalj: Om du tittar närmare på flaggan ser du att det inte är dagens svenska flagga som vajar i vinden - det är flaggan från när Sverige och Norge var i union (1814-1905)!
